subsystems.summary: Lines 1-398 hold the whole presentation layer. A tokenized dark theme sits on :root (16-30) and the CSS is grouped by region: header, stage, rails, intel panel, brief, log, setup, splash, toast, then one mobile @media block at 308-323. The static HTML skeleton (336-395) is a flex column (#top header, #stage with #rail | #mapwrap | #panel, #mobilebar) plus fixed #splash/#toast overlays, and the script fills in all dynamic content. Dependencies are Google Fonts, Leaflet 1.9.4 (css 12, js 396) and satellite.js 5.0.0 (397), all from CDNs with pinned versions but no SRI. The helpers serve.js and serve.py are small, readable, dependency-free twins. Each serves the folder on 127.0.0.1 and exposes /proxy?url=, which checks an exact-match https host allowlist, forwards only `accept` and `x-windy-api-key`, and adds `ACAO: *`. The .bat probes for py -3 / python / node / bun in that order, and the .vbs re-launches the .bat minimized. I confirmed every issue below by running sandboxed copies of the helpers (in %TEMP%, never the project folder) and the page at 1280/940/880/390 px widths.

key_functions.name: :root design tokens (colors, fonts, --top-h/--rail-w/--panel-w)
key_functions.role: Single source of theme colors and layout sizes. Script line 427 reads a fixed list of these back via cssVar() to color canvas glyphs.

key_functions.name: #top header flex row
key_functions.role: Fixed-height (56px) nameplate bar: brand, clocks, stat chips, audio button, alerts button, search. No wrapping or overflow handling on desktop.

key_functions.name: #rail / #panel side columns
key_functions.role: Fixed-width flex siblings of #mapwrap on desktop (296 + 372 px). They become absolute bottom sheets in the mobile query.

key_functions.name: @media (max-width:900px) mobile block
key_functions.role: Folds the rails into bottom sheets, shows #mobilebar, sets --top-h:auto. Its 900px threshold disagrees with the JS (860px).

key_functions.name: HTML skeleton #app/#stage/#mobilebar/#splash
key_functions.role: Static containers that the script populates (views, legend, layers, brief, detail, log, setup, audioPop, welcome).

key_functions.name: serve.js proxy()
key_functions.role: Node relay: parses url, checks https + ALLOWED_HOSTS, forwards 2 headers, fetch() with redirect:'follow', 60 s timeout, buffers the body, replies with ACAO:*.

key_functions.name: serve.js serveFile()
key_functions.role: Static file server. Does decodeURIComponent + path.join + a string-prefix containment check.

key_functions.name: serve.js request router (http.createServer)
key_functions.role: Routes OPTIONS, /proxy, '/' redirect and static files. Logs relay hosts.

key_functions.name: serve.py Handler.do_GET / Handler.proxy
key_functions.role: Python twin of the router and relay (urllib with default redirect following, manual gzip/deflate decode). Static files come from SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, which handles traversal safely.

key_functions.name: serve.py Server + main()
key_functions.role: ThreadingTCPServer with allow_reuse_address=True. Prints a 'port busy' message on OSError and opens the browser after 0.6 s.

key_functions.name: Start Open Overwatch.bat runtime probe chain
key_functions.role: Tries py -3, python, node, bun in order and runs the first that answers. Pauses on exit.

key_functions.name: Relay (cross-ref, html)
key_functions.role: Page side of the helper contract: NEEDS_RELAY host list (483), local detection, /proxy?ping=1 health check, wrap() for the URL.

key_functions.name: applyLayoutMode / openSheet (cross-ref, html)
key_functions.role: JS side of responsive layout: uses innerWidth <= 860 to choose sheet mode and toggles .hidden on #rail/#panel.

subsystems.extension_points:
Adding a data feed that lacks CORS takes three edits that must stay in sync: add the host to NEEDS_RELAY (html 483), and to ALLOWED_HOSTS in both serve.js 12-21 and serve.py 12-21. If the feed needs an auth header, also add it to FORWARD_HEADERS in both servers (serve.js 22, serve.py 22). Missing any one edit fails at runtime with "host not in the helper's allowlist" (403) or "blocked by browser security (CORS)". A shared hosts list, or the servers fetching it from the page, would make this a one-line change.

Adding a layer color: add a token to :root (17-24), then add its name to the hard-coded array at html 427 so the canvas renderer can read it.

Adding an Intel tab: add a button[data-tab=X] in .tabs (370-375) and a section.tab#tab-X (376-379). showTab() (831) is generic, so no JS change is needed.

Adding a header chip: add a span.chip to .stats (340-346). But the header already overflows at every desktop width below about 1500px, so the header layout needs a fix first (a wrap/priority scheme or a container query).

Adding a third mobile sheet: openSheet() (833) only knows about #rail and #panel, so it needs code changes.

The CSS itself is easy to extend: tokens throughout, section comments, a few broadly reused component classes (.btn, .chip, .pill, .flag, .kv, .item). The main obstacles are the single 2085-line file and responsive rules split between CSS (900px) and JS (860px).

data_sources.name: Google Fonts (Big Shoulders Display, Barlow, IBM Plex Mono)
serve.js allowlist: ADS-B aggregators (adsb.lol, airplanes.live, adsb.fi, adsb.one)
serve.js allowlist: NASA FIRMS (key in URL path)
serve.js allowlist: CelesTrak / tle.ivanstanojevic.me (allowlisted but never relayed: not in NEEDS_RELAY, ivanstanojevic unused)

subsystems.quality_notes:
Strengths: the CSS is well organized for a single file. It has a real token layer on :root, section comments, consistent component classes, prefers-reduced-motion support, safe-area insets, and canvas colors read back from the same tokens (html 427), so retheming is mostly a :root edit. The HTML skeleton is minimal and semantic enough (aside/nav/section, aria-labels, an SVG icon sprite), and the script owns all dynamic content, so the skeleton rarely needs touching. The helpers are short, dependency-free, bound to 127.0.0.1, https-only, exact-match allowlisted, and forward only two request headers. The architecture is sound for a personal tool.

Weaknesses:
- The responsive design was tuned only for the extremes (wide desktop, ~390px phone). Everything in between has confirmed defects: header overlap at 901-1500px, both sheets showing at 861-900px, a 272px map at 940px. On phones the audio popover is offscreen and 'Center on me' can't be tapped.
- The relay's security model is "allowlist only". It does not check Origin or Host, and it follows redirects without re-validation.
- serve.js has a one-request crash and a prefix-match path check.
- The Node and Python helpers are mostly at parity, but not fully:
  - Node relays any HTTP method as GET; Python returns 501.
  - Python serves directory listings; Node returns 404.
  - Python double-binds the port on Windows.
  - If gzip decoding fails, Python silently forwards compressed bytes with no Content-Encoding (serve.py 86-92), which the page reports as 'not JSON'.
- In the .bat, a Python 2 'python' on PATH passes the line-7 probe; serve.py then fails, and `goto :done` skips the Node fallback.
- The relayed-host list is copied three times and has already drifted.

None of this blocks building on the project: each issue has a small, local fix. I'd fix the serve.js crash/containment bugs and the 860/900 breakpoint before adding features, and generate the allowlist from one source before adding more relayed feeds.

confirmed_issues.description: serve.js crashes the whole helper on any request path with malformed percent-encoding. The exception is thrown synchronously inside the request listener, nothing catches it, and the process exits.
confirmed_issues.evidence: serve.js:47 `const rel = decodeURIComponent(pathname)` has no try/catch. It is called from the 'request' handler at 62. Reproduced: GET http://127.0.0.1:18787/%E0%A4%A gives `URIError: URI malformed at serveFile (serve.js:47)`, Node exits, and the next /proxy?ping=1 gets connection refused. Any web page the user has open can trigger it with , and so can a typo; after that every relayed feed (aircraft, OpenSky, NHC, GDELT, NYC cams, FIRMS, Windy) goes dark until restart. Related: line 53 `fs.createReadStream(file).pipe(res)` has no 'error' listener, so a read error after stat (e.g. EBUSY while an editor saves the HTML) is also an uncaught exception. serve.py does not have this problem (SimpleHTTPRequestHandler answers 404).
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. I ran a sandbox copy of serve.js with the browser-opener removed. GET /% returned ECONNRESET, the process exited with code 1 (stack ends in parserOnIncoming), and the next /proxy?ping=1 got ECONNREFUSED. Line 47 decodeURIComponent has no try/catch and Node does not catch exceptions thrown in a 'request' listener. The unhandled createReadStream 'error' at line 53 is the same class of crash but rarer. I rate it low, not medium: it only affects the Node path (the .bat tries Python first), the trigger is an unusual URL (a typo with a stray %, or a hostile page, which current Chrome gates behind its local-network permission), and a restart fixes it. The fix is a one-line try/catch.

confirmed_issues.description: serve.js's path containment check is a bare string prefix, so files in sibling folders and sibling files whose names start with the folder name are served.
confirmed_issues.evidence: serve.js:48-49: `path.normalize(path.join(DIR, rel))` then `if (!file.startsWith(DIR))`. A '%2f'-encoded '..' survives URL normalisation and is decoded at 47. Reproduced with a sandbox copy: GET /..%2fopen-overwatch-secret%2fsecret.txt returned 200 with the sibling file's contents. Realistic case: the user's open-overwatch.zip sits next to the folder in Downloads, and /..%2fopen-overwatch.zip passes the check. Exposure is local (static responses carry no ACAO, so a cross-origin read needs DNS rebinding, and neither server checks Host). Fix: compare against DIR + path.sep, or use path.relative. serve.py is not affected.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed with a sandbox layout of s/ow (the helper), s/ow-secret/secret.txt and s/ow.zip. GET /..%2fow-secret%2fsecret.txt returned 200 SECRET and /..%2fow.zip returned 200 ZIP. /..%2fother.txt was correctly refused with 403, so only siblings whose path starts with the folder name leak. The URL parser keeps the %2f segment as one segment, line 47 decodes it, and line 49's startsWith(DIR) has no trailing separator. It is low because the helper binds 127.0.0.1 only and static responses carry no ACAO, so another site needs DNS rebinding to read the bytes. The fix is to compare against DIR + path.sep.

confirmed_issues.description: Any web page can use the relay, and the relay follows redirects to any host or scheme without re-checking the allowlist. It also forwards the Windy key header across those redirects. Today the allowlist is the only boundary, and each new host added makes it weaker.
confirmed_issues.evidence: serve.js:27 and serve.py:58 send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on /proxy, and OPTIONS (serve.js:59, serve.py:40) allows any header. There is no Origin or Host check, so any site the user visits can fetch http://127.0.0.1:8787/proxy?url=... and read the result. That spends the user's per-IP ADS-B/GDELT budgets, which the page itself warns about at html 2073. serve.js:39 `fetch(target, { redirect: 'follow' })` and serve.py:80 `urlopen` (default HTTPRedirectHandler) only validate the first hop. If any of the 12 allowlisted hosts has an open redirect (or a future one does), a hostile page can make the helper fetch http://127.0.0.1:<port>/... or LAN/metadata addresses and read the body back through ACAO:*. Both stacks also forward custom headers on cross-host redirects (urllib copies all non-content headers; undici strips only authorization/cookie), so x-windy-api-key would go to the redirect target. Fix: redirect:'manual' and re-check each Location against the allowlist; reject requests whose Origin is not the helper's own origin.
confirmed_issues.verification: Part of this is real. serve.js:27 and serve.py:58 send ACAO:* on /proxy, and neither server checks Origin or Host. That header is not even needed for normal use, because the page is served same-origin by the helper, so another origin can read relayed responses wherever the browser lets public sites reach loopback. The impact is small: all allowlisted hosts serve public data, so the realistic harm is spending the user's per-IP ADS-B/GDELT budget. The SSRF and header-leak parts are hypothetical: they need an open redirect, or a cross-host redirect from api.windy.com, on an allowlisted host, and none was identified. So I rate it as a hardening gap, not a medium issue. Fixes worth doing: drop ACAO:* (or limit it to the helper's own origin and 'null'), and use redirect:'manual' with a re-check of each hop.

confirmed_issues.description: The CSS mobile breakpoint (900px) and the JS layout breakpoint (860px) disagree. Between 861 and 900px wide, both bottom sheets are shown on top of each other over the map.
confirmed_issues.evidence: CSS 308 `@media (max-width:900px)` turns #rail and #panel into absolute bottom sheets (315) and shows #mobilebar. JS applyLayoutMode (html 835) and Detail.show (794) use `window.innerWidth <= 860`. Above 860, JS removes .hidden from both rails. Measured at 880px: #rail and #panel are both display:flex, position:absolute, at the identical box (0,266, 880x496), while #mobilebar highlights 'Map'. The Layers sheet is fully hidden under the Intel sheet and 62% of the map is covered.
confirmed_issues.verification: Real. CSS line 308 switches to the mobile layout at max-width 900px, while applyLayoutMode (835) and Detail.show (794) use innerWidth <= 860. Between 861 and 900px, applyLayoutMode removes .hidden from both #rail and #panel. Line 315 then makes both absolute bottom sheets in the same box, and #panel paints over #rail because it comes later with the same z-index. Meanwhile #mobilebar still shows 'Map' as the active button. I rate it low because the band is only 40px wide, and tapping any mobile-bar button calls openSheet() and fixes the state. Fix by sharing one breakpoint, e.g. matchMedia('(max-width:900px)').

confirmed_issues.description: The desktop header has a fixed height and no wrap or overflow rule. Below about 1500px wide, the brand block shrinks to near zero and its title/tagline draw on top of the clocks and stat chips. At the low end of desktop widths, the map between the two fixed rails becomes a sliver.
confirmed_issues.evidence: #top (46) is a single-row flex with height:var(--top-h)=56px. .brand (49) has min-width:0 but no overflow:hidden, and its h1/.tag are white-space:nowrap (54, 56), so it can shrink while its text overflows. Measured at 1280px: .brand box ends at x=355, but the tagline spans x=293-479 over .clocks (369-504). In a screenshot, 'LIVE PICTURE FROM OPEN FEEDS' is printed over the UTC/LOC clocks. At 940px: .brand is 62px wide, the h1 spans 51-282 and the tagline 293-479, overlapping both .clocks (90-217) and .stats (231-537). With --rail-w 296 + --panel-w 372 (28), #map is only 272px wide at 940px.
confirmed_issues.verification: Real from the code. .brand (49) has min-width:0 and is the largest shrinkable flex item in the fixed 56px #top row. Its h1 (54) and .tag (56) are white-space:nowrap, and nothing hides the overflow. The other items cannot shrink much: the chips have a 58px min-width each (about 306px total), #btnAudio has min-width:150, and #search has min-width:130. I estimate the row's natural width at about 1,550-1,600px. Below that the brand box shrinks while its text spills over .clocks/.stats. This covers 1280, 1366, 1440 and 1536px laptops, matching the reviewer's measurement of the tagline drawn over the clocks at 1280. I could not re-measure in a browser here, but the flex arithmetic supports it. The narrow map at around 940px is a design squeeze, not a separate bug. It is cosmetic, but it shows on the most common laptop widths, so medium stands.

confirmed_issues.description: On phones the soundtrack popover opens with its top cut off above the viewport. Its position depends on --top-h, which the mobile query sets to 'auto', which makes the calc() invalid.
confirmed_issues.evidence: 68: `#audioPop{position:absolute; top:calc(var(--top-h) + 6px)}`. 309: `:root{--top-h:auto}` inside the mobile query. calc(auto + 6px) is invalid at computed-value time, so top becomes auto. The popover then takes the static position of an abspos child in an align-items:center flex container (#top), i.e. it is centered vertically on the header. Measured at 390x800: header height 163, popover rect top = -85px (computed top '-84.98px'). Its first ~85px (title row and mode buttons) is offscreen, and body{overflow:hidden} (33) means it cannot be scrolled into view.
confirmed_issues.verification: Real. Line 309 sets --top-h:auto under the mobile query, so line 68's top:calc(var(--top-h) + 6px) becomes calc(auto + 6px). That is invalid at computed-value time, so top falls back to auto. Nothing in JS positions the popover: togglePop (1903) only flips .hidden. With top and bottom both auto, the abspos #audioPop sits at its static position inside the align-items:center flex container #top (position:relative). It is therefore centered on the header and starts above the viewport whenever it is taller than the header, and body overflow:hidden (33) keeps the cut-off part unreachable. On phones this hides the title row and the Generated/Radio mode buttons. Fix: give the mobile query its own explicit top, e.g. top:100%.

confirmed_issues.description: On phones, Leaflet's scale and attribution controls paint over the Layers bottom sheet and swallow taps on its footer buttons.
confirmed_issues.evidence: The mobile #rail sheet has z-index 1000 (127) and comes before #mapwrap in the DOM (353 vs 363). Leaflet's .leaflet-top/.leaflet-bottom also use z-index 1000 in the same root stacking context, so they paint on top because they come later. Measured at 390px with the Layers sheet open: elementFromPoint at the center of #btnLocate ('Center on me', 14-100 x 729-754) returns `.leaflet-control-scale-line`, so the button cannot be tapped, and 261/1235 sampled points of .railfoot hit Leaflet controls. #panel is unaffected because it comes after #mapwrap.
confirmed_issues.verification: Real. In the mobile query, #rail is position:absolute with z-index:1000 (127, 315) and sits before #mapwrap in the DOM (353 vs 363). Neither #mapwrap, #map nor .leaflet-container creates a stacking context: none of them sets a z-index, filter or transform. So Leaflet 1.9.4's .leaflet-top/.leaflet-bottom (z-index:1000) compete in the same context and win on DOM order. Their .leaflet-control children have pointer-events:auto. The scale control (bottom-left, 14px margins, 115) and the attribution (bottom-right) sit exactly where .railfoot ends, because both #rail and #map are bottom-aligned in #stage. They therefore paint over the left and right of the Layers footer and take taps meant for its controls (basemap select, Center on me, Pause). No JS hides these controls on mobile. #panel is unaffected because it comes after #mapwrap. Fix: give the mobile sheets z-index 1001 or more.

confirmed_issues.description: The relay host list lives in three hand-synced copies that have already drifted, and the launch messages list the wrong set of relayed feeds.
confirmed_issues.evidence: html 483 NEEDS_RELAY, serve.js 12-21 and serve.py 12-21 ALLOWED_HOSTS. The servers allowlist celestrak.org and tle.ivanstanojevic.me as 'orbital data fallbacks', but neither is in NEEDS_RELAY, ivanstanojevic is never referenced in the page, and CelesTrak is always fetched directly (1115, 1187). No fallback exists. Conversely, NEEDS_RELAY routes FIRMS and Windy through the helper, but 'Start Open Overwatch.bat' lines 13-14, README 16-18 and the page's own log text (2050-2051) say only aircraft/OpenSky/NYC/NHC/GDELT need it. Adding a new CORS-less source means editing all three lists, or it fails at runtime with 403 'host not in the helper's allowlist' or a CORS block.
confirmed_issues.verification: Real, but there is no runtime failure today. Every host in NEEDS_RELAY (483) is in both servers' ALLOWED_HOSTS, so nothing currently gets a 403. The drift is real but harmless. celestrak.org and tle.ivanstanojevic.me are allowlisted as 'orbital data fallbacks', but CelesTrak is fetched directly (1115, 1187) and ivanstanojevic is never referenced, so no fallback exists. The user-facing text in the .bat (13-14), the README (16-18) and the boot log (2050-2051) lists the relayed feeds without FIRMS and Windy. For a project that will keep adding sources, three hand-synced lists are a real maintenance hazard: forgetting one gives a 403 or CORS failure at runtime. It is a maintainability issue, not a bug, so low.

confirmed_issues.description: On Windows, serve.py's allow_reuse_address=True lets a second instance bind the same port that is already in use. The 'Port is busy' handling never fires, and two helpers silently share 8787.
confirmed_issues.evidence: serve.py:97 `allow_reuse_address = True` sets SO_REUSEADDR, which on Windows permits binding over an active listener. Reproduced: a second instance on the same port printed 'Open Overwatch helper on ...' instead of the busy message at 108-109, and netstat showed two LISTENING sockets (PIDs 16656 and 25960) on 127.0.0.1:18788. This happens easily with the minimized .vbs launcher, because the user can't see the first instance and double-clicks again. Since the .bat prefers Python (line 6), this is the default Windows path. Fix: set allow_reuse_address=False on win32 (or use SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE).
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. On this machine (py -3 = 3.13.14), two copies of serve.py (opener removed) on port 18793 both printed 'Open Overwatch helper on ...', and netstat showed two LISTENING sockets with different PIDs. socketserver.server_bind sets SO_REUSEADDR when allow_reuse_address is True (line 97), and Windows lets that bind over an active listener. So the 'Port is busy' branch (108-109) never runs on Windows. I rate it low because both copies serve identical content. It only causes confusion when an older copy, or an unrelated program, already holds 8787. Fix: allow_reuse_address = sys.platform != 'win32'.

confirmed_issues.description: The minimized launcher fails silently when the folder path contains '&' or '^', because cmd strips the outer quotes.
confirmed_issues.evidence: 'Start Open Overwatch (minimized).vbs' line 6 builds `cmd /c "<dir>\Start Open Overwatch.bat"`. With special characters inside, cmd falls back to stripping the first and last quote and splits the path. Reproduced with an identical Run line: folder 'ow & co' gave exit=1 and the .bat did not run, while 'ow plain' and 'ow (1)' worked. Window style 7 means the user sees nothing. Wrapping in an extra pair (`cmd /c ""<path>""`) fixed it in the same test.
confirmed_issues.verification: Real by cmd.exe's documented /c quote rules. Line 6 builds cmd /c "<dir>\Start Open Overwatch.bat". When a special character (&, ^ and others) appears between the quotes, cmd strips the outer quotes. An unquoted & then splits the command and ^ is consumed as an escape, so the .bat never runs, and window style 7 hides the error. Parentheses are listed as special too, but they still work, because cmd retries unquoted paths at each space; that matches the reviewer's 'ow (1)' result. I did not re-run it because this sandbox's long temp path breaks cmd. Folder paths containing & are uncommon, so low. Fix: wrap the path in an extra pair of quotes, cmd /c ""<path>"".

confirmed_issues.description: Third-party scripts load from CDNs without Subresource Integrity, in a page that keeps API keys in localStorage.
confirmed_issues.evidence: 396 (Leaflet JS, cdnjs) and 397 (satellite.js, jsdelivr), plus Leaflet CSS at 12, have no integrity/crossorigin attributes. The versions are pinned, so adding SRI hashes is a cheap fix. A tampered CDN response would run with access to the Windy, FIRMS and aisstream keys the Setup tab stores via Store (ow.* keys in localStorage, html 444-445).
confirmed_issues.verification: Accurate: lines 12, 396 and 397 load pinned Leaflet 1.9.4 and satellite.js 5.0.0 without integrity or crossorigin attributes. The same origin's localStorage holds the user's Windy, FIRMS and aisstream keys (Store, 444-445). Exploiting it needs a CDN compromise, so this is cheap hardening rather than a functional defect. The Google Fonts stylesheet (11) cannot take SRI, and that is fine.

rejected_issues.description: A full-viewport film-grain overlay with mix-blend-mode and backdrop-filter rails add compositing work to every repaint of a page that redraws its canvas continuously.
rejected_issues.reason: This is an unmeasured performance guess about an intentional visual effect, not a demonstrated defect. Repaints do happen: requestDraw runs at 2 Hz (770), the CSS sweep animation runs constantly (51), and the 60 fps visualizer only runs while music plays (1908). But the reviewer gives no profile, frame-time data or observed stutter. The body::after grain is a static, pointer-events:none layer at 5.5% opacity, and modern GPU compositors handle that cheaply. On desktop the rails sit beside the map, not over it, so their backdrop blur has nothing changing behind it. Worth profiling if jank appears on low-end phones, but as stated it is a speculative style or performance preference.

subsystems.summary: Lines 401-840 are the whole runtime core, written as global singletons in one inline script. There are small helpers (esc/fmt/geo math), a localStorage wrapper (Store), Log/toast/Sound, a network layer (Net.fetch with timeout, an opt-in per-host spacing queue, and routing through a localhost /proxy for hosts listed in NEEDS_RELAY), and the Leaflet map with its basemaps. Everything clickable is drawn by one custom canvas layer (Glyphs) in screen coordinates. It redraws the whole scene, rebuilds a flat hit list on every draw, and contains hard-coded blocks for satellites, ships, balloons and aircraft, plus a generic 'Points' block for static point sets. Layers are plain objects registered with Layers.add. Persisted on/off state and options feed a sidebar built once by UI.build. Polling is done by feed(def, opts) objects ticked by a 1-second setInterval scheduler, with a fixed error-retry interval, 3x slower polling in hidden tabs, and a nudge after panning for view-dependent feeds. Selection is the globals Sel and Detail, with a per-kind renderer table that produces HTML strings. Map clicks go through Glyphs.hitTest first, then cable proximity, then the probe popup. The design is compact and consistent, and adding a static point feed is cheap. Moving-object types, click arbitration and the scheduler/fetch handshake have real bugs and hidden coupling (listed below).

key_functions.name: esc / fmt / haversine / destination / hexA
key_functions.role: Shared helpers: HTML escaping, number/time formatting, great-circle math (destination is used for aircraft dead reckoning), and hex-to-rgba conversion used by every canvas fill (it only accepts #rgb or #rrggbb).

key_functions.name: Store
key_functions.role: localStorage wrapper with an 'ow.' prefix and JSON encoding; swallows errors. Holds view, basemap, layer state, opts, keys, the custom relay setting and TLE caches.

key_functions.name: Log.add
key_functions.role: Prepends a row to the Feed log (capped at 400). kind 'alert' also raises a toast and a sound. Messages are escaped unless opts.html is set. Calls made before INIT sets Log.el are dropped.

key_functions.name: Relay
key_functions.role: Decides whether a URL needs the relay (hostname exactly in NEEDS_RELAY), builds the relay URL (local helper /proxy?url= or a custom template with {url}), and pings the helper once at boot.

key_functions.name: Net.slot / Net.fetch
key_functions.role: fetch wrapper: optional per-key serial spacing (throttle/gap), relay rewriting, AbortController timeout, HTTP error to Error message (including a 429 hint), and errors mapped to 'timeout' / 'CORS or offline' / 'not JSON'. Every feed uses it.

key_functions.name: setBasemap
key_functions.role: Swaps the tile layer group chosen from the BASEMAPS table (Esri/OSM/OpenTopoMap/NASA GIBS) and persists the choice.

key_functions.name: sunPosition / terminatorRing
key_functions.role: Low-precision solar ephemeris used by the day/night layer, the probe and the satellite detail.

key_functions.name: Points
key_functions.role: Registry of static point sets: define(setId, layerId, {minZoom}), set(setId, items), clear, find. Items are drawn by Glyphs.draw in definition order.

key_functions.name: Glyphs (L.Layer)
key_functions.role: The single overlay canvas in overlayPane. _reset resizes and repositions it on moveend/zoomend/resize/viewreset. draw() paints point sets, then satellites, ships (clustered below z5), balloons and aircraft (dead-reckoned, with a label budget), and rebuilds this._hits.

key_functions.name: Glyphs.hitTest
key_functions.role: Linear scan of the hit list that picks the object for hover and click. Its scoring is broken (see issues).

key_functions.name: Layers
key_functions.role: Layer registry: add(def) sets def.on from persisted state or def.default; set(id,on) persists, calls enable/disable, clears def.points, resets feed status and redraws; opt/setOpt hold persisted options; migrate() is a one-off options migration.

key_functions.name: UI.build / UI.refreshLayer / UI.pills
key_functions.role: Builds the layer sidebar once, grouped by the fixed UI.groups list, with an optional def.sub(el) control row. Shows feed status dot, count, error text and last-update time per row.

key_functions.name: requestDraw
key_functions.role: Coalesces redraw requests into one requestAnimationFrame. A separate 500 ms interval (line 770) forces a full redraw whenever any aircraft or satellites exist.

key_functions.name: feed
key_functions.role: Creates the feed record {interval, errorInterval, fetch, status, count, lastOk, err, nextAt, running, viewDependent, minZoom} and attaches it to def.feed.

key_functions.name: runFeed
key_functions.role: Runs one fetch: skips if the layer is off or a fetch is already running, idles below minZoom, sets status loading/ok/error, and afterwards overwrites nextAt to interval or errorInterval.

key_functions.name: scheduler tick + view nudge
key_functions.role: 1-second interval that runs any due feed (hidden tab waits interval*3). The moveend handler at 788 pulls viewDependent feeds forward to about 1.5 s.

key_functions.name: Detail
key_functions.role: Selection and side panel: show(kind,obj,id) sets Sel and renders Detail.renderers[kind](obj) as an HTML string. head/kv/links are helpers. Line 802 re-renders air/sat/ship/balloon details every 2 s.

key_functions.name: Hover.move + map click handler
key_functions.role: Tooltip from hitTest. Click arbitration order is glyph hit, then cluster fly-to, then Detail.show, then cableHit, then Probe.open.

key_functions.name: showTab / openSheet / applyLayoutMode
key_functions.role: Tab switching and the mobile bottom-sheet layout, plus ResizeObserver and polling fallbacks that keep Leaflet sized.

subsystems.extension_points:
THE LAYER/FEED CONTRACT, as the code enforces it:
(1) Register with `const ly = Layers.add({id, group, name, desc, color, shape?, default?, points?, sub?(el), enable?(), disable?()})`. This must run before INIT (line 2036). UI.build at 2039 runs once, and layers added later never appear in the sidebar. `group` must exactly match one of UI.groups (727), or the layer is registered (and can be on) but never shown. `id` is persisted in ow.layers and interpolated into a DOM id and a CSS selector (737/749), so keep it [a-z0-9_]. enable() runs on toggle-on and once at INIT for layers already on (2064), not at add time. disable() runs only on toggle-off. `desc` may be mutated by the fetch and is re-shown on refresh. Per-layer options go through Layers.opt/setOpt. Defaults are hard-coded in the object literal at 717, and schema changes need an ad-hoc migrate() flag like cam_v2.
(2) Polling: `feed(ly, {interval: seconds, fetch: async (force) => {...}, errorInterval?, viewDependent?, minZoom?, startDelay?})`. The fetch must THROW to report failure; the message becomes the red row text and one Log.error. It must set `ly.feed.count` itself and call Points.set or requestDraw itself. It must NOT set ly.feed.status or ly.feed.nextAt, because runFeed overwrites both after the promise settles (780-781). A layer that is not polled but wants a status dot has to fabricate a feed object by hand (see line 1570). Use `Net.json/Net.text(url, {timeout, throttle: 'hostkey', gap})` for every request.
(3) Rendering, path A (static points, the easy path): `Points.define(setId, ly.id, {minZoom})`, set `points: setId` on the def so toggle-off clears it, and call `Points.set(setId, items)`. Item fields: {lat, lon, r (number or z=>number), color (MUST be #hex because of hexA), alpha, fillAlpha, shape: 'tri'|'sq'|circle, stroke, lw, halo, label, labelZoom, kind, obj, tip}.
Path B (lines/polygons): `const g = lineLayer(ly)` (1238), then add L.polyline/L.geoJSON with `renderer: vecRenderer, interactive: false`. If you leave a vector interactive, its click also triggers the map probe (see the NWS issue).
Path C (moving objects): there is no generic mechanism. Add a Map to Dyn (580), write a new hard-coded block inside Glyphs.draw (579-704) with its own Layers.on gate, choose a hit `kind`, add the kind to the live re-render list at 802 and to the Hover label table at 813, and make disable() purge your entries.
(4) Click/detail: set `Detail.renderers[kind] = obj => html`. Renderers must escape every dynamic value themselves: Detail.kv values (799) are inserted raw, and Detail.links (800) does not check the URL scheme, so use esc() and isHttp(). Points selection is matched by object identity, so either reuse objects across polls or expect the selection ring to drop after a refresh.
(5) CORS-blocked source: add the host to NEEDS_RELAY (483) AND to ALLOWED_HOSTS in both serve.js (12) and serve.py (12). The relay is GET-only and forwards only x-windy-api-key/accept, so a POST body or an Authorization header is lost.
(6) Optional wiring: push parsed data into World.* (1239) and edit Brief.render to surface it in the brief, add the id to PRESETS, and add a legend entry.
EASY: a new point or GeoJSON feed is about 15 lines following the earthquake template (1242-1257), and status, error display, persistence, hidden-tab throttling and toggle handling come for free. HARD: everything lives in one 2,000-line global script with no modules, tests or build. Any exception thrown at top level while a new layer is being defined aborts everything after it, including INIT. Moving-object types require editing the core renderer, hover table and re-render list. The scheduler cannot cancel an in-flight fetch, and the fetch cannot reschedule itself. Hit-testing and click arbitration are split across three systems (canvas hits, cableHit, Leaflet interactive vectors) with no shared priority.
