subsystems.quality_notes:
Strengths: the core is small, readable once you get past the very long lines, and consistent. The feed/registry pattern gives every layer persistence, a status dot, error text, hidden-tab throttling and toggle handling for free. A static point layer is about 15 lines following the earthquake template. Net.fetch centralises timeouts, relay routing and error wording, and the helper's host allowlist and 127.0.0.1 binding are sensible. The single shared canvas is a good choice for thousands of objects.

Weaknesses that matter for building on it:
(1) Everything is in one global script with no modules, tests or build. Any exception thrown while a new feature is being defined aborts the rest of the script, including INIT.
(2) The scheduler and fetch contract is implicit and leaky. Fetches must throw rather than set status, cannot reschedule themselves, and cannot be cancelled. Requests made while a fetch runs are lost, and error retry is pinned to at least the success interval.
(3) The renderer is a monolith. Each moving-object type is a hard-coded block with its own visibility rule, and adding one means touching Dyn, Glyphs.draw, the hover kind table and the live re-render list.
(4) Hit-testing is incorrect (wrong object picked when symbols overlap), and click handling is split across canvas hits, cableHit and Leaflet interactive vectors.
(5) Selection is by object identity while most feeds rebuild objects.
(6) HTML is assembled from strings, and whether a value gets escaped depends on the caller (Detail.kv values are raw, Detail.links has no scheme check). That already produced a real XSS path from SondeHub data.
(7) The full scene redraws at 2 Hz and FIRMS points are uncapped.

None of this blocks extension, and most fixes are local: hitTest scoring, repositioning the canvas in draw(), a generation counter or AbortController in runFeed, escaping in kv and links, and a static/dynamic canvas split. They should be done before adding many more layers, because each new layer copies the current conventions.

confirmed_issues.description: hitTest picks the wrong object whenever symbols overlap. It compares `d < bd + x.r` and then stores `bd = d`, so a later-scanned item replaces the current best whenever it is within its own radius of the previous best distance, even if it is farther from the cursor. The scan runs from the top layer down, so bottom layers win.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `if (d < bd + x.r) { bd = d; best = x; }`. Reproduced in node with the same function. (a) Cursor exactly on an aircraft drawn over an M7 quake whose centre is 10 px away (quake hit r = 16.4, pushed at 628): result is 'quake'. (b) At zoom 9 or more (aircraft r = 9), cursor exactly on plane A with plane B 8 px away and earlier in the hit list: result is 'air B'. (c) Open ground 25 px from an M7 quake: result is 'quake', so the probe never opens. Clicking traffic near airports or over large symbols therefore opens the wrong detail. Fix: score by `d - x.r` and keep the minimum.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed at line 601. `if (d < bd + x.r) { bd = d; best = x; }` compares each item's distance against the previous best distance plus the new item's radius. Hits are pushed in draw order: points (628), then sats, ships, balloons, and aircraft last (699). The scan runs from the end, so aircraft are tested first. With the cursor on an aircraft (d=0), an M7 quake 10 px away (r = 2 + 6*2.4 = 16.4, line 1252) passes 10 < 0 + 16.4 and takes the selection. Two planes 8 px apart at zoom 9 or more (r=9) behave the same way. Wrong-object selection is real, but it only happens where symbols overlap and is a UX bug with no data loss, so medium rather than high. Case (c), the 14 px slack around a large symbol, is closer to intended tolerance.

confirmed_issues.description: Glyphs are drawn in container coordinates onto a canvas living in overlayPane, which moves with the map pane during a drag. The canvas is only repositioned in _reset (moveend), so any redraw during a drag paints every glyph shifted by the drag distance a second time.
confirmed_issues.evidence: _reset sets the canvas at containerPointToLayerPoint([0,0]) only on 'moveend zoomend resize viewreset' (593/599). draw() uses m.latLngToContainerPoint (609), which already includes the pane offset d, and the canvas element is itself offset by d, so glyphs appear at correct + d. The 500 ms interval at 770 forces draw() whenever aircraft or satellites exist (air_mil and sats are on by default), so during a slow pan or inertia every aircraft, ship and quake jumps by the drag delta and snaps back on release. Fix: call L.DomUtil.setPosition(...) at the start of draw().
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. The canvas sits in overlayPane, inside the mapPane that Leaflet translates during a drag or inertia. It is repositioned to containerPointToLayerPoint([0,0]) only in _reset, which runs on 'moveend zoomend resize viewreset' (593, 599). draw() paints at latLngToContainerPoint (609), which already includes the current pane offset, so mid-drag glyphs land at the correct point plus the drag delta. The 500 ms interval (770) calls draw during drags whenever aircraft or satellites exist, and both are default-on, so glyphs visibly jump and then snap back on moveend. Nothing in the code handles 'move' events.

confirmed_issues.description: runFeed unconditionally overwrites f.nextAt after the fetch settles, and it silently drops runs requested while a fetch is in flight (`if (... f.running) return`). Reschedule requests made during a fetch are lost: the moveend nudge (788), re-enabling a layer (723 sets nextAt = 0), forced option changes (e.g. 1243), and AirSweep's own `lyAirLocal.feed.nextAt = 0` (1004).
confirmed_issues.evidence: `f.nextAt = Date.now() + f.interval * 1000` runs after `await f.fetch(force)`. Scenario: FIRMS fires (interval 900 s, viewDependent, fetch up to 60 s). The user pans to a new region while a fetch is in flight, the nudge sets nextAt to now + 1.5 s, then the old fetch resolves with the previous view's fires and sets nextAt to +900 s, so the new area stays empty or stale for 15 minutes. Likewise, clicking a different earthquake feed pill during a fetch calls runFeed(..., true), which returns immediately, and the old dataset stays up for 5 minutes. AirSweep's 'sweep again right away' at 1004 is always replaced by +8 s.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Line 780 sets `f.nextAt = Date.now() + f.interval*1000` after `await f.fetch()`, which overwrites any nextAt change made while the fetch was in flight: the moveend nudge (788) and AirSweep's `nextAt = 0` (1004, which runs inside the fetch itself, so it is always overwritten). runFeed(f, true) from the quake pills (1243), news (1325) and camera pills (1447) returns immediately at 777 when f.running is set, so that request is dropped. FIRMS reads map.getBounds() at fetch start (1549) with interval 900, so panning during a slow fetch leaves fires for the old view for 15 minutes. Caltrans camera loads are multi-MB and sequential, which makes the in-flight window common.

confirmed_issues.description: A fetch that handles its own errors gets its error status overwritten with 'ok'. Sats.reload catches CelesTrak failures and sets feed.status = 'error' (1140/1142), but it resolves normally, so runFeed marks the layer ok, clears err, and schedules the next try 7,200 s later.
confirmed_issues.evidence: If all CelesTrak groups fail at startup (timeout or 403 rate-limit), Dyn.sats is empty and Log.error fires, but runFeed sets `f.status = 'ok'; f.err = ''` and nextAt to +2 h (interval 7200, line 1235). The satellites row shows a green dot with no count, and nothing retries for 2 hours (6 hours if the tab is hidden) unless the user toggles the layer.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Sats.reload catches per-group failures (1136) and sets ly.feed.status = 'error' with err text (1140/1142), then resolves normally. The feed fetch (1235) awaits it, and runFeed (780) then sets status = 'ok', err = '' and nextAt = +7200 s. loadGroup (1113-1118) has no fallback to a stale cache on failure. If CelesTrak rate-limits or times out at startup, the default-on Satellites row shows a green dot with no count, and nothing retries for 2 h (longer in a hidden tab) unless the user toggles a group or the layer.

confirmed_issues.description: The default error retry is `Math.max(interval, 30)`, so a failed long-interval feed waits at least a full success interval. There is no exponential backoff and no short cap, and the hidden-tab rule adds interval*2 on top.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Submarine cables and landing stations use interval 86400 with no errorInterval (1433/1435). If the first load times out (60 s timeout against a large mirror), the row stays red with '✕ timeout' for 24 h (72 h in a background tab) unless the user toggles it. Every future slow feed inherits this. Conversely, fast feeds that hit HTTP 429 retry at a fixed 30 s with no growth.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. errorInterval defaults to Math.max(interval, 30) (773). Cables and landing stations use interval 86400 with no errorInterval (1433, 1435), so one failed first load stays red for 24 h. The hidden-tab rule at 786 adds 2*interval on top. Low because both layers are off by default (1419, 1421), and toggling the layer resets nextAt to 0 (723).

confirmed_issues.description: Detail.kv inserts values into innerHTML unescaped (only keys are escaped), so every renderer must escape values itself. The balloon renderer passes SondeHub's crowd-sourced uploader_callsign through raw, which is a stored-XSS path into the page origin that holds API keys and the relay setting.
confirmed_issues.evidence:
`
${v}
` at 799; `['Heard by', b.uploader]` at 1535, where b.uploader = t.uploader_callsign from api.v2.sondehub.org (1539), a free-text field set by any station that uploads telemetry. A callsign like `` runs when a user clicks that balloon. The script can read ow.keys (Windy/aisstream/FIRMS keys, line 1925) and persist ow.proxy (486) so that all relayed requests, including FIRMS URLs carrying MAP_KEY, go to an attacker relay. The OSM renderer (1559) shows the author escapes in some places but not others.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Detail.kv writes values raw into innerHTML (`<dd>${v}</dd>`, 799), and Detail.render assigns the result to innerHTML (796). The balloon renderer passes ['Heard by', b.uploader] raw (1535), and b.uploader is t.uploader_callsign from api.v2.sondehub.org (1539), a free-text field that any telemetry uploader sets. frequency, temp, pressure and humidity are also interpolated unescaped. Clicking that balloon runs injected markup in the page origin, which holds the API keys and the ow.proxy relay setting in localStorage. Medium because the balloons layer is off by default and a click is needed.

confirmed_issues.description: The renderer draws all of Dyn.air (679) and Dyn.balloons (667) with no Layers.on check, and all Dyn.ships whenever either ship layer is on (649). Visibility depends on each layer's disable() purging its entries, and toggling off does not cancel an in-flight fetch that re-adds them.
confirmed_issues.evidence: air_emg (1032) has no disable(), so unchecking 'Emergency squawks' leaves squawk-only aircraft drawn with pulsing red rings until Air.prune drops them about 240 s later. Toggling air_mil off while its 15 s fetch is in flight: disable() deletes the military aircraft, then the resolving fetch calls Air.ingest and re-adds them, and they stay visible on an unchecked layer for up to 150 s (prune TTL, line 901). With only ships_fi on, any leftover 'ws' ships still render.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. The aircraft block (679) draws every Dyn.air entry with no Layers.on check, and the balloon block (667) does the same. air_emg (1032) defines no disable(), and air_local's disable deliberately keeps emerg aircraft (1024), so squawk-only aircraft stay drawn after unchecking until prune drops them (240 s emergency TTL, 901). air_mil's fetch (1030) calls Air.ingest unconditionally, so a fetch that resolves after disable() re-adds the military aircraft until the 150 s TTL. Real, but it clears itself within minutes, so low. The ship part of the claim is weaker, since ships_ws disable deletes the ws entries and closes the socket.

confirmed_issues.description: The detail panel renders the object captured at click time (Sel.obj), and point-set selection rings match by object identity (619). Feeds that rebuild objects each poll leave the selection stale: the ship and balloon panels refresh every 2 s with frozen data, and quake rings vanish after a refresh.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Ship feeds create a new object per update (Dyn.ships.set at 1510 and 1520), and balloons are cleared and recreated (1538-1539). The 2 s timer at 802 calls Detail.render(), which runs r(Sel.obj) on the old object: position, speed and course never change and 'Fix age' keeps climbing while the glyph (matched by Sel.id at 653) moves on the map. The 'Center' button flies to the old position. Quakes create fresh `p` objects every 300 s (1251), so `Sel.obj === it.obj` fails and the ring disappears while the panel still shows the quake. The 2 s full innerHTML rewrite also clears any text selection in the panel (for example a hex code being copied).
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Detail.render calls r(Sel.obj) (796), and the 2 s timer (802) re-renders ship and balloon panels. Ship feeds store a new object per update (1510, 1520) and balloons are cleared and recreated (1538-1539), so the panel keeps showing the click-time position, speed and course while 'Fix age' climbs. Meanwhile the map glyph, matched by Sel.id (653, 670), moves on. Quake objects are rebuilt every 300 s (1251), so `Sel.obj === it.obj` at 619 fails and the selection ring disappears. Aircraft are mutated in place (886), so they are unaffected.

confirmed_issues.description: The whole scene, including every static point set, is re-projected and repainted every 500 ms whenever any aircraft or satellite exists. The hit list is rebuilt each frame and scanned linearly on every mouse move.
confirmed_issues.evidence: The interval at 770 calls requestDraw; draw() loops over every item of every Points set (615-631), with up to three latLngToContainerPoint calls, a hexA() string parse, an arc fill and a stroke each. FIRMS returns every VIIRS detection in the view with no cap (1552), and a zoom-5 view over an active fire region can return tens of thousands of rows, all repainted twice a second. Hover runs hitTest over all of them every 40 ms (820). _reset also reallocates the DPR-scaled canvas on every moveend (598), and zoom triggers both zoomend and moveend, so it draws twice. A separate static-layer canvas, redrawn only on data or view change, would remove most of this.
confirmed_issues.verification: The behaviour is as described. The 500 ms interval (770) runs whenever aircraft or satellites exist, and draw() re-projects and repaints every Points item each time (615-631). FIRMS has no item cap (1552), and _reset reallocates the canvas on both zoomend and moveend. The cost only shows with very large sets: FIRMS is off by default, needs a key and requires zoom 5 or more. The linear hit test is cheap even at 20k items. This is a real scalability concern for future layers rather than a present correctness bug, so low.

confirmed_issues.description: Map click arbitration does not account for interactive Leaflet vectors. Clicking an NWS warning polygon fires its own Detail.show and then bubbles to the map click handler, which finds no glyph and also opens the Probe popup with its weather and geocoder requests.
confirmed_issues.evidence: NWS polygons are created with L.geoJSON (interactive by default) and `g.on('click', () => Detail.show('nws', ...))` at 1365, with no stopPropagation. Leaflet then fires the map 'click', and lines 824-827 fall through to Probe.open(e.latlng), so both the NWS detail and a probe popup appear (plus Open-Meteo and Photon calls).
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. NWS polygons are built with L.geoJSON, which is interactive by default, and get a click handler with no stopPropagation (1365), contrary to the 'non-interactive' comment at 1237. In Leaflet 1.9 the canvas renderer fires the layer click through map._fireDOMEvent with the map in the target chain, and Path bubblingMouseEvents defaults to true, so the map 'click' (823) also fires. hitTest finds nothing, so Probe.open (827) opens a popup and starts the Open-Meteo and Photon requests on top of the NWS detail.

confirmed_issues.description: showTab only re-renders the Brief when `window.Brief` exists, but Brief is a top-level `const` (1635), which never becomes a window property. The check is always false.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Switching to the Brief tab, or using the '← Brief' backlink rendered at 796, shows whatever the 5 s timer (1733) last rendered instead of fresh content. The same `window.X` pattern will silently fail for any other const singleton.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. The app script is a classic script (398, not a module), and `const Brief` at 1635 is a global lexical binding, not a window property. Nothing assigns window.Brief (window.OW.Brief at 2082 does not count), so the check at 831 is always false. Brief.render returns early unless the brief tab is active (1641), so after switching to the tab the content stays stale or empty for up to 5 s, until the timer at 1733 fires. Low impact.

confirmed_issues.description: Below zoom 5, ships are collapsed into one bubble per source placed at the arithmetic mean of all their lat/lon values. For the global aisstream feed (or any set spanning the antimeridian) that centroid has no ships near it.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `g.lat += s.lat; g.lon += s.lon` and then the mean at 663. With aisstream subscribed to a world view, the bubble lands at the average of ships in, say, the North Sea and the South China Sea, and clicking it (825) flies to zoom 6 over empty ocean or land.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Line 662 takes the arithmetic mean of lat/lon per source. aisstream subscribes to the whole view bbox at zoom < 5, falling back to the full globe when the view crosses the antimeridian or is wider than 360° (1524), and ws ships linger for 15 minutes after a pan (1529). A view spanning both sides of the Atlantic, or one that includes earlier panned regions, puts the bubble where there are no ships, and the click at 825 flies there. The Digitraffic source is regional and unaffected. Low.

confirmed_issues.description: Boot has no error containment. The 'Leaflet failed to load' fallback at 2079 is dead code, because L is dereferenced at 533 and the script aborts there first. Any top-level exception, including one in a newly added layer definition, kills INIT and leaves the splash stuck.
confirmed_issues.evidence: If cdnjs is blocked or offline, `L.map(...)` at 533 throws ReferenceError. The user sees an empty UI and never gets the friendly message at 2079. The window error handler (2078) is registered last and only surfaces messages matching /satellite|Leaflet|\bL\b/. The persisted ow.view is passed to setView (532-534) without validation.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. If the cdnjs Leaflet script (396) fails to load, `L.map(...)` at 533 throws a ReferenceError and the rest of the classic script never runs. The `typeof L === 'undefined'` fallback at 2079 is unreachable, and the splash buttons (2058) are never wired, so the splash stays stuck. The error listener at 2078 is registered after everything else. Low because it only matters when the CDN is blocked or the machine is offline.

confirmed_issues.description: The NASA GIBS imagery date is computed once at page load, so a long-running dashboard (the scheduler is designed to keep polling in background tabs) keeps showing increasingly old VIIRS and night-lights imagery and an outdated basemap label.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `const imgDate = ... Date.now() - 36*3600e3` is baked into BASEMAPS.viirs/night URLs and names (548-549). After three days open, the 'NASA VIIRS true color' basemap still shows the image from the load date.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. imgDate is computed once at load (539) and baked into the VIIRS and night-lights URLs and names (548-549), and nothing recomputes it. A tab left open for days keeps the load-day imagery and label. Minor.

rejected_issues.description: Detail.links escapes the URL but does not restrict the scheme, so each caller must remember isHttp(). GDACS and camera renderers pass feed-supplied URLs unchecked.
rejected_issues.reason: It is true that Detail.links does not filter the URL scheme. The URLs cited, however, come from official HTTPS APIs: GDACS from gdacs.org (1287), and cameras from TfL, NYC DOT, Caltrans, LTA and Fintraffic, mostly with hardcoded c.link values (1461-1478). A javascript: URL would need one of those upstreams to be compromised, and even then the links are target=_blank rel=noopener. The genuinely crowd-sourced feeds (EONET sources, GDELT) are already filtered with isHttp. This is defense-in-depth, not a demonstrable defect.

rejected_issues.description: The relay host list is maintained by hand in three places, and the relay does not support everything Net.fetch accepts. Net.fetch takes method, body and headers, but the helpers only proxy GET and forward only x-windy-api-key/accept.
rejected_issues.reason: There is no present failure. NEEDS_RELAY (483) is a subset of ALLOWED_HOSTS in both serve.js and serve.py (both also allow celestrak.org and tle.ivanstanojevic.me). No current caller sends a relayed POST or any header other than x-windy-api-key/accept (1479). The rest is a hypothetical future limitation and a maintenance note, not a defect in the current code.

subsystems.summary: Lines 841-1235 hold the aircraft and satellite engines. Aircraft: `Air` puts three aggregators that use the ADSBx-v2 JSON shape (adsb.lol, adsb.fi, airplanes.live) behind per-source pacing. A 429 response slows that source down and pauses it for 60 s. `Air.ingest` turns responses into mutable records in `Dyn.air`, with flags, trails and TTL pruning. `AirSweep` covers the visible map with a hexagonal grid of 250 nm query circles, up to 30, nearest the center first, and both sources pull tiles from one shared queue. The canvas renderer (lines 679-703) moves each aircraft forward from its last fix using speed, track and `seen_pos`. Separate feeds cover worldwide military (/v2/mil), emergency squawks (which also raise alerts), an OpenSky global snapshot and Planespotters photos. Satellites: `Sats` downloads CelesTrak GP groups as TLE text, caches them in localStorage for 2 h, parses them, and runs SGP4 (satellite.js) in a Blob Web Worker that sends positions back in a Float32Array every 1-3 s. If the worker fails, the same work runs on the main thread. It also draws ground tracks and footprints, estimates elevation and next pass, and searches by name. The design is sound overall, but there are real concurrency and state bugs: dropped reloads, a stale selection after reload, a tile-queue race, and emergency alerts that never fire for aircraft in view. There are also feed-status and caching problems.

key_functions.name: Air.getFrom
key_functions.role: One request to a single source through the Net.slot pacing lane; checks the cooldown, and on HTTP 429 calls on429 (gap x1.5, 60 s pause). Used only by the sweep.

key_functions.name: Air.get
key_functions.role: Tries the sources in order for mil, squawk, hex, callsign and reg queries. Rebuilds the request path inline (duplicating Air.path at 855). Lookups get their own throttle lane.

key_functions.name: Air.ingest
key_functions.role: Merges ADSBx-v2 JSON (ac or aircraft) into Dyn.air records. Computes the mil, interesting, PIA, LADD, emergency and low-NIC flags and adds a trail point when the aircraft has moved more than 150 m. Returns the number of aircraft that had a position.

key_functions.name: Air.prune
key_functions.role: Removes stale records by TTL: OpenSky 400 s, emergency 240 s, military 150 s, civil max(75 s, 3 x last pass + 30 s). Runs every 3 s from the interval at 925, which also updates the counters, history and follow.

key_functions.name: Air.roleOf / Air.notable
key_functions.role: Guesses a role from the ICAO type with the ROLES regex list (911-920). Used by Detail, Brief and Fun.

key_functions.name: Detail.renderers.air
key_functions.role: Builds the HTML for the aircraft detail panel: flags, photo, key-value rows, Center/Trail/Follow buttons as inline onclick, and outbound links.

key_functions.name: AirSweep.plan
key_functions.role: Hexagonal grid of 463 km circles over the view (latitude clamped to ±80), sorted by distance from the center and capped at MAX_TILES. Builds this.key, which is order-sensitive.

key_functions.name: AirSweep.pass
key_functions.role: One worker per source pulls tiles from a shared index `next`. Stops when the key changes (map moved), calls next-- to hand back the tile on cooldown or block errors, and sets passMs and the layer description.

key_functions.name: feed(lyAirEmg)
key_functions.role: Polls squawk 7700 every 45 s and alternates 7500/7600. Raises Log.alert for aircraft that were not already known as emergencies.

key_functions.name: feed(lyOpenSky)
key_functions.role: Maps the OpenSky states/all tuples into the same record shape with src='opensky'. Skips aircraft whose existing record came from ADS-B.

key_functions.name: Photos.html / Photos.fetch
key_functions.role: Planespotters thumbnail lookup by hex, cached in a Map with in-flight de-duplication. Re-renders the detail panel when the selected aircraft's photo arrives.

key_functions.name: SAT_WORKER_SRC
key_functions.role: Worker source in a template string: importScripts satellite.js, 'load' builds satrecs, 'prop' returns lat, lon, alt and speed per satellite in a transferable Float32Array.

key_functions.name: Sats.loadGroup
key_functions.role: Downloads a CelesTrak GROUP as TLE, with a localStorage cache keyed tle.<group> and a 2 h freshness check (CelesTrak's download policy).

key_functions.name: Sats.parse
key_functions.role: Parses 3-line TLE text into objects: NORAD id via parseInt of columns 3-7, inclination, period, eccentricity, international designator, epoch.

key_functions.name: Sats.reload
key_functions.role: Rebuilds byId and Dyn.sats from all enabled groups plus ad-hoc search results, then posts 'load' to the worker. Guarded by this.loading and catches all errors itself.

key_functions.name: Sats.startWorker / mainThread
key_functions.role: Creates the worker from a Blob URL. onerror switches to a main-thread copy of the same SGP4 loop. Starts the 1 s prop timer.

key_functions.name: Sats.onMessage
key_functions.role: Matches worker positions to objects by NORAD id, updates the chip, requests a redraw, and redraws the selected satellite's track every 30 s.

key_functions.name: Sats.prop
key_functions.role: Asks the worker for positions every 1 s (every 3 s above 2,500 objects) unless a request is already in flight; skipped while the tab is hidden.

key_functions.name: Sats.drawTrack
key_functions.role: Main-thread SGP4 ground track over about one orbit, split where it crosses the antimeridian, plus a footprint circle at the object's current lat/lon.

key_functions.name: Sats.nextPass / elevation / above
key_functions.role: Observer geometry: spherical-earth elevation from the sub-point; next pass by stepping SGP4 every 30 s over 24 h with ecfToLookAngles.

key_functions.name: Detail.renderers.sat
key_functions.role: HTML for the satellite detail panel: groups as flags, orbital elements, buttons to center, draw the track and clear it.

key_functions.name: feed(lySats)
key_functions.role: Runs every 2 h: reloads if not ready, empty, or any group's cached TLEs are older than 2 h.

subsystems.extension_points:
Adding another aggregator that uses the same ADSBx-v2 JSON shape takes edits in about six separate places:
1. Base URL in AIR_SRC (842).
2. Path builders in AIR_PATHS (843-847); set optIn:true if it needs permission.
3. Starting gap in Air.gap (849).
4. NEEDS_RELAY (483), if the host sends no CORS headers.
5. ALLOWED_HOSTS in serve.js (line 12) and serve.py (line 12).
6. The hard-coded pill list in lyAirLocal.sub (1013), which is separate from AIR_SRC.

Air.order() then adds the new source to the sweep's shared tile queue and to the failover in Air.get automatically.

A source with a different data shape needs its own normalizer, like the OpenSky feed (1050-1062). Expect to touch the string special-cases for 'opensky' in prune (901), lyAirLocal.disable (1024) and lyOpenSky.disable (1049), because records carry no proper source or owner model.

A new aircraft layer (a watchlist, helicopters only, an alert rule) is Layers.add({id, group:'Air', ...}) plus feed(layer, {interval, fetch: async () => Air.ingest(await Air.get(kind, ...), tag)}). Two catches:
- The canvas renderer (679-703) draws every record in Dyn.air whether or not any layer is on. Aircraft are hidden only by deleting records in disable(). Any filter-style layer therefore needs a predicate added to Glyphs.draw, or more delete-based disable() code.
- There is no hook after ingest. New alert rules have to go inside Air.ingest or in a feed, and must avoid the 'known' dedupe trap described in the issues.

Satellites are easy at the edges. A CelesTrak group is one entry in Sats.GROUPS (1103), using CelesTrak's GROUP name; heavy:true draws it dimmed. Pass prediction and elevation (1194-1207) already exist, so a 'passes over me' list or a visibility filter is cheap.

Switching element sources (Space-Track, SupGP, OMM/JSON) means replacing loadGroup and parse. parse assumes 3-line TLE text and parseInt'd 5-digit catalog numbers. Alpha-5 IDs would come out as NaN and all collapse into one Map key.

A bigger change (more objects, other per-object outputs such as look angles) means editing SAT_WORKER_SRC and the copy in mainThread (1155-1157) in step.

What makes all of this harder:
- Very dense lines with several statements each.
- HTML built as strings with inline onclick handlers that call globals.
- Implicit coupling to runFeed's status and nextAt rules (780).
- One shared Tracks group (804) used by aircraft trails, satellite tracks and the Locate marker.
- No tests.

data_sources.name: adsb.lol ADS-B API (point, mil, squawk, hex, callsign, registration)
adsb.fi open data API (point via lat/lon/dist, mil, sqk, hex, callsign, registration)
airplanes.live API (opt-in only; answers 403 without written permission)
OpenSky Network global state vectors (anonymous, polled every 15 min)
Planespotters.net airframe photos by ICAO hex
CelesTrak GP element sets by group (TLE)
satellite.js 5.0.0 SGP4 library, loaded inside the worker with importScripts (runtime CDN dependency)

subsystems.quality_notes:
The engineering ideas are better than the code layout. Strong points:
- Adaptive per-source pacing with a 429 cooldown, and a shared tile queue so a second aggregator can take over.
- A hexagonal circle cover sorted from the center outward, with wrap handling.
- Dead-reckoning that accounts for seen_pos.
- SGP4 in a Blob worker with a transferable Float32Array, and a main-thread fallback.
- Positions matched by NORAD id, so the load/prop message ordering cannot misassign them.
- A TLE cache that follows CelesTrak's 2 h policy.
- Inline comments that explain why, not just what.

Weak points:
- Lines are extremely dense, often 5-10 statements each.
- Logic is duplicated: Air.path vs the inline path code in Air.get; the source pills (1013) vs AIR_SRC; SAT_WORKER_SRC vs mainThread; NEEDS_RELAY vs the serve.js and serve.py allowlists. serve.js/py also allowlist tle.ivanstanojevic.me, which the page never uses.
- Source special cases are string compares ('opensky').
- Aircraft visibility works by deleting records rather than by a render filter.
- rec.mil is recomputed from whichever aggregator answered last, while the 'mil' tag sticks in rec.tags. Aggregators with different databases could make an aircraft's colour flip between passes.
- Feeds that catch their own errors break runFeed's status model.
- HTML is built as strings with raw values and inline onclick handlers that call globals.
- There are no tests, and the worker code is an untyped template string.
- parse() assumes 5-digit catalog numbers, so moving to OMM/JSON later will need a parser change.

Most of the bugs found are about shared mutable state and timing: the shared next counter, the loading guard, Sel.obj identity, nextAt being overwritten. That is the area to firm up before adding features. Specifically:
- a pending-reload flag in Sats.reload;
- rebinding Sel.obj after reload;
- a per-tile retry queue instead of next--;
- letting fetch request an immediate rerun;
- escaping in Detail.kv;
- IndexedDB for the TLE cache.

None of this needs a rewrite. The structure (Layers.add + feed + Detail.renderers + Dyn + one canvas) can be extended once these issues are fixed.

confirmed_issues.description: Sats.reload() quietly drops any call made while a reload is already running. Group changes made during a load are ignored until the next feed run, up to 2 h later.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `if (this.loading) return;`. Callers that rely on a reload actually happening: the group pills (1229), Presets.apply (1585), Fun.followIss (1619) and searchByName (1190, which `await`s a no-op and returns found[0] before it is in byId). Scenario: enable Starlink (a big download with a 90 s timeout), then click GPS before it finishes. The second reload returns at once, the GPS pill shows 'on', but GPS objects never appear. The lySats feed has interval 7200 and only reloads when the list is empty or a cache entry is stale, so the missing group shows up only about 2 h later. Searching for a satellite during a load toasts 'Loaded X' but byId.get(s.id) is undefined (2031), so nothing is selected or drawn.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Line 1130 returns at once while `loading` is set. The running reload captured `groups = this.groupsOn()` at 1132. Pill clicks (1229) store a new filtered array through setOpt, so the in-flight loop never sees the added group. The only other trigger is the lySats feed (1235), which runs again at now+7200 s (780). A pill clicked during a load stays 'on' with no data until the next feed run or another toggle. searchByName (1190) awaits the no-op and returns found[0]. At 2031, byId.get(s.id) is undefined, so it toasts 'Loaded X' and selects nothing. The in-flight reload does pick up `this.adhoc` at 1138, so the satellite appears later, but the selection still fails.

confirmed_issues.description: CelesTrak failures show as a healthy (green) layer, and failed groups are not retried for 2 h, because reload() handles its own errors and runFeed then overwrites the status.
confirmed_issues.evidence: reload() records per-group failures and sets `ly.feed.status = 'error'` (1140), and its outer try/catch (1142) means it never throws. runFeed (780) then runs `f.status = 'ok'; f.err = ''; f.nextAt = now + 7200 s`. Scenario: CelesTrak times out or refuses a repeat download at startup. The layer row turns green with count 0, the error appears only in the Log tab, and no retry happens for 2 h (errorInterval would also default to 7200).
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Per-group failures are caught at 1136, and the outer try/catch at 1142 swallows everything else, so reload() never throws. Line 1140 sets status 'error', but when the feed called it, runFeed (780) then sets status 'ok', clears err and sets nextAt to now+7200 s; errorInterval is never used. The row shows a green dot. The error goes only to the Log tab (1141, Log.error does not toast). The splash (2053) reports 'online · 0'. There is no automatic retry for 2 h. A partial failure also looks fully healthy.

confirmed_issues.description: No alert or sound fires for an emergency squawk in the area the user is watching. The sweep ingests the aircraft first, so the emergency feed treats it as already known.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `known = new Set([...Dyn.air.values()].filter(a => a.emerg)...)` and alerts fire only for hexes not in `known` (1041). Air.ingest sets `rec.emerg` from the squawk for every source (893), including the 8 s sweep. Scenario: an aircraft in view squawks 7700. The sweep picks it up within seconds and marks it emerg. Up to 45 s later the squawk feed sees it in `known` and skips Log.alert. Only emergencies outside the swept view raise alerts. Aircraft flagged only through the `emergency` field (for example 'nordo', 'minfuel') with a normal squawk never alert at all.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. No other code path alerts on emergencies: a grep finds Log.alert only at 1042, 1254 and 1366, and the other two are not aircraft. ingest (893) sets rec.emerg from the squawk for every tag, so emerg is set by the sweep (every pass, about 45 s per tile), the mil feed (every 15 s, worldwide) and OpenSky. Line 1036 builds `known` from Dyn.air before the squawk query, and 1041 skips known hexes. An in-view aircraft that a sweep tile refreshes first gets no alert. Neither does any military aircraft, which the 15 s mil feed almost always sees first. Aircraft with a non-'none' `emergency` field but a normal squawk are never returned by the squawk endpoints, so they never alert either.

confirmed_issues.description: Sweep tiles are only handed back to the queue for cooldown or blocked errors. Any other error from one source (403, 5xx, timeout) uses up that tile for the pass. Choosing airplanes.live without permission leaves holes in coverage.
confirmed_issues.evidence: The requeue regex is `/blocked by browser|no helper|cooling down|pausing/`. Other errors are pushed to errs and the worker moves on to the next tile. The UI offers airplanes.live as a pill (1013), and Air.order() puts the preferred source first, so the pass runs three workers. airplanes.live answers 403 fast and takes a tile every 2.5 s like the others, so about a third or more of the tiles are never queried each pass. The description then reads something like '20/30 tiles'. The comment's promise that 'the other covers everything' holds only for 429s.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Line 997 requeues only on /blocked by browser|no helper|cooling down|pausing/. getFrom (856-860) does not rewrite 403 or 5xx messages, so such an error is pushed to errs and the worker takes the next tile. Air.order() (854) puts the preferred source first even when it is opt-in. Its worker starts first in srcs.map and therefore always takes tiles[0], the center tile. A source that fails fast, such as airplanes.live answering 403, keeps pulling tiles on its own 2.5 s lane. The center tile and about a third of the others are lost on every pass. The `!done` check at 1003 only throws when every tile failed. The same holds for any persistent non-429 error from adsb.fi in the default configuration.

confirmed_issues.description: Handing a tile back with `next--` on the shared counter is a race. It skips one tile and fetches another twice. When the preferred source is in cooldown, the skipped tile is always tile 0, the one at the map center.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Both workers start in srcs.map(worker). Worker A (preferred, cooling) takes tiles[0] (next=1), and getFrom rejects. Before A resumes, worker B takes tiles[1] (next=2). A's catch runs `next--` (next=1) and returns. B finishes tile 1 and then takes tiles[1] again. Tile 0 is never fetched. The same happens to whichever tile was in flight when a 429 arrives mid-pass. For the 60 s cooldown after any 429 on the preferred source, aircraft at the center of the view go stale.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed by tracing the microtask order. Worker A runs synchronously: `tiles[next++]` takes tile 0, then getFrom throws inside the async function and A suspends on the rejected promise. srcs.map then starts worker B, which takes tiles[1] (next=2) and suspends in Net.slot. A's catch then runs `next--` (next=1) and returns. When B finishes, it takes tiles[1] again. Tile 0 is never fetched. Air.order() does not filter cooling sources, so this repeats on every pass for the 60 s cooldown after a 429 on the preferred source (853). A 429 in the middle of a pass likewise drops the in-flight tile and duplicates another worker's tile.

confirmed_issues.description: After any satellite reload (a group toggle, the 2-hourly refresh, a search), the selected satellite's detail panel and auto footprint freeze. reload() creates new objects while Sel.obj still points at the old one.
confirmed_issues.evidence: reload builds new objects (`objs.set(t.id, {...t, lat:null,...})`) and replaces byId and Dyn.sats. onMessage (1163) updates only `this.byId.get(id)`. Sel.obj is never rebound. Detail.render (802) keeps showing the old object's frozen Sub-point and Altitude. onMessage calls `drawTrack(Sel.obj)` every 30 s (1165), which redraws the footprint circle at the frozen lat/lon while the canvas ring (matched by Sel.id) moves on. Scenario: select the ISS, click any group pill, and the panel stops updating.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. reload (1135, 1139) builds new objects and replaces byId and Dyn.sats. onMessage (1163) updates only `this.byId.get(id)`. Sel.obj is assigned only in Detail.show (794). The 2 s Detail.render (802) keeps rendering the old object, whose Sub-point and Altitude are frozen. Every 30 s, 1165 calls drawTrack(Sel.obj), which redraws the footprint circle (1184) at the frozen lat/lon. Meanwhile the canvas ring, matched by Sel.id at 638, follows the new object. For the ISS the footprint ends up hundreds of km off within a minute. Any pill toggle, preset or search triggers this.

confirmed_issues.description: Detail.kv (799) inserts row values as raw HTML. The aircraft renderer passes strings from third-party JSON straight in (r, t, flight, squawk, category, country) and puts a.hex unescaped into inline onclick JavaScript (961).
confirmed_issues.evidence:
`
${v}
` with no esc(). The rows include ['Registration', a.r], ['Type', a.t], ['Callsign', a.flight], ['Country', a.country], and `onclick="Air.trail('${a.hex}')"`. These values come from the aggregators, OpenSky, or a user-configured custom relay (Relay.custom). If any of them returns e.g. `"r":""`, the script runs on the 127.0.0.1:8787 origin, where `ow.keys` (Windy, aisstream and FIRMS keys) sits in localStorage and /proxy is reachable. Real ADS-B character sets make this unlikely today, but every future renderer inherits the trap. The satellite renderer passes o.intl the same way (1212).
confirmed_issues.verification: The code issue is real. Detail.kv (799) emits `<dd>${v}</dd>` without esc(). Feed strings a.r, a.t, a.flight, a.squawk, a.category and a.country reach it through rows 946-952. a.hex is placed unescaped inside a single-quoted onclick (961). Exploiting it requires an aggregator, OpenSky or a user-configured relay to return HTML. ADS-B callsigns are decoded from a 6-bit charset, so normal data cannot carry '<'. The impact is limited to a localhost origin holding a few third-party API keys. It is a real latent trap for future renderers, but low severity today.

confirmed_issues.description: 'Moved mid-pass: sweep again right away' never takes effect. runFeed overwrites nextAt after the fetch returns. Because the tile key depends on order, even a small pan that only re-sorts the same tiles aborts a pass.
confirmed_issues.evidence: pass() sets `lyAirLocal.feed.nextAt = 0` and returns, then runFeed (780) sets `f.nextAt = Date.now() + 8000`. The moveend nudge (788) also runs during the pass and is overwritten the same way. Passes take about 40 s, so most pans happen mid-pass, and the new view waits roughly the in-flight request plus 8 s. `this.key` (982) joins tiles in distance-sorted order, so any pan that reorders them, including the 3 s auto-pan while following an aircraft (931), aborts the pass and starves the outer tiles. Aborted passes also record a tiny passMs, which shrinks the civil TTL in prune (901) for the next pass.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. 1004 sets nextAt=0, then runFeed (780) overwrites it with now+8000 once fetch resolves. The 788 moveend nudge made during a pass is overwritten the same way. A pan therefore waits for the in-flight request plus 8 s, not 'right away'. The key at 982 depends on distance order, so a pan that only reorders nearly equidistant tiles, including follow pans after each new fix (931), still aborts the pass. The short passMs from an aborted pass lowers civTtl in prune (901), down to its 75 s floor. The practical effect is a few seconds of extra latency plus some starvation of outer tiles while following an aircraft.

confirmed_issues.description: Follow pans to the last raw fix, not to the dead-reckoned position where the icon is drawn, so the followed aircraft sits off-center and jumps.
confirmed_issues.evidence: The follow interval runs `map.panTo([a.lat, a.lon])`, while Glyphs.draw (685-686) draws the aircraft at destination(a.lat, a.lon, track, gs x dt), with dt up to 150 s including seen_pos. A 450 kt jet with 15 s of staleness is drawn about 3.5 km from the center, then snaps back on each fix. Each pan also fires moveend, which re-plans the sweep and pulls the sweep feed's nextAt forward (788, 1027).
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. 931 pans to the raw [a.lat, a.lon], while 685-686 draw the aircraft at destination(..., gs*dt), with dt up to 150 s including seen_pos. For the followed aircraft (center tile) a new fix arrives roughly once per pass plus the 8 s gap, about 45 s. The icon drifts several km from center (about 10 km at 450 kt) and the map jumps forward on each new fix. It is a cosmetic and UX issue.

confirmed_issues.description: The search caller (2029) assumes `d.ac[0]` exists and has a position. Air.ingest is more tolerant: it accepts `data.aircraft` and skips entries without a position.
confirmed_issues.evidence: ingest uses `data.ac || data.aircraft` and counts only entries with lat/lon. The search then uses `d.ac[0].hex`. If the first entry has no position while a later one does, Dyn.air.get(hex) is undefined and the lookup silently fails. If a source answers with `aircraft`, `d.ac[0]` throws a TypeError, which the catch at 2030 swallows. Either way the user is told 'No aircraft ... matched'. ingest should return the hexes it actually stored.
confirmed_issues.verification: The code mismatch is real but rarely triggered. ingest (879-881) accepts data.aircraft and skips entries without a position. The caller (2029) indexes d.ac[0].hex. If the first entry lacks a position and a later one has one, Dyn.air.get(hex) is undefined and the lookup falls through to 'No aircraft ... matched'. If a response used `aircraft`, d.ac[0] would throw, and the catch at 2030 silently swallows it. Callsign and registration lookups normally return a single match, so this is an edge case.

confirmed_issues.description: The auto ground-track refresh calls Tracks.clear() every 30 s. That wipes everything else in the shared Tracks group, including the Locate 'you are here' marker and any aircraft trail.
confirmed_issues.evidence: onMessage → drawTrack (1165) → `Tracks.clear()`. Locate.go (1606) adds its circleMarker to the same Tracks.group. Scenario: select a satellite with 'auto ground track' on, press Locate, and the position marker disappears within 30 s.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. drawTrack (1174) calls Tracks.clear(), which empties the whole shared Tracks.group (804). Locate.go (1606) adds its 'you are here' circleMarker to that same group. sat_tracks defaults to true (717). With a satellite selected, onMessage (1165) runs drawTrack every 30 s, so the location marker disappears within 30 s. This is a minor UX defect.

confirmed_issues.description: The role guess labels the Dassault Falcon 50 (ICAO type FA50) as 'fighter / attack'. The fighter regex includes FA50 and is checked before the bizjet regex, which also lists it.
confirmed_issues.evidence: ROLES is checked in order. 'fighter / attack' (915) contains FA50 and 'bizjet / VIP' (919) contains it too, so roleOf returns 'fighter / attack'. Falcon 50s are common military VIP transports, so the detail flag (937) and the Brief role tally (1649) mislabel them. The same list also files bombers (B52, B1, B2, TU95) under 'fighter / attack'.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. In ICAO Doc 8643, FA50 is the Dassault Falcon 50; the KAI FA-50 is filed as T50. roleOf (921) checks ROLES in order, and 'fighter / attack' (915) contains FA50 before 'bizjet / VIP' (919) does. Military Falcon 50s are therefore labeled as fighters in the detail flag (937) and in the Brief role tally (1649). Grouping bombers under 'fighter / attack' is a labeling choice, not a bug.

confirmed_issues.description: Any photo-lookup failure, including a timeout or 429, is cached as 'no photo' for the rest of the session.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `catch (e) { this.cache.set(hex, null); }`, and html() returns '' when the cached value is null, so the lookup is never retried. One network hiccup while clicking an aircraft hides its photo until the page reloads. The cache Map also never shrinks.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. The catch at 1077 caches null for any error, including a timeout, a 429 or a relay hiccup. html() (1070) returns '' for null and never calls fetch again, so the photo stays hidden until the page reloads. The cache only grows by one entry per aircraft clicked, so the 'never shrinks' part is negligible. The missing retry after a transient error is real but low impact.

rejected_issues.description: TLE text for every group ever enabled is cached in localStorage and never evicted. Heavy groups can fill the origin's quota, after which every Store.set in the app fails silently. Uncached groups then re-download on every reload, and CelesTrak refuses repeat downloads within 2 h.
rejected_issues.reason: The stated scenario does not reach the quota. Each group's key is overwritten in place (1117), so growth is bounded by the 20 fixed groups. Starlink is roughly 9-11k objects x ~174 chars, about 1.7-1.9M chars. Starlink + OneWeb + GEO + the two debris groups total about 2.1M chars, and all 20 groups about 2.3-2.5M. Chromium allows about 5M chars per origin. No other code stores anything large in localStorage: the grep shows only small prefs. The failure path is already handled: 1117 checks Store.set and logs a warning, and Setup has a 'clear TLE cache' button (1941). The re-download chain depends entirely on the quota being exceeded, which this scenario does not do.

rejected_issues.description: Every 500 ms the renderer moves every aircraft forward along a great circle before culling off-screen ones. With the OpenSky snapshot (~10k global aircraft) plus sweep and Starlink, this is tens of thousands of trig-heavy steps per frame on the main thread.
rejected_issues.reason: This is a performance observation, not a defect with a concrete failure. destination() is about 8 transcendental ops. Even for about 10-12k aircraft per redraw at 2 Hz (770), that is a few ms per frame, negligible. At the zooms where many aircraft are on screen, the cost is canvas drawing of visible glyphs, which culling before dead-reckoning does not change. The linear hit-test scan over about 20k entries every 40 ms is also sub-millisecond. The reporter concedes it is a 'scaling ceiling more than a bug'.

rejected_issues.description: User lookups use a separate throttle lane (`src + ':lookup'`), so they are not paced against that source's sweep, mil and squawk traffic. Searches can push a source over its per-IP limit and pause it for the sweep for 60 s.
rejected_issues.reason: This is an intentional, documented trade-off. The comment at 867 says lookups get their own lane so they are not stuck behind the sweep. The lookups run sequentially (2029 awaits each Air.get) and are paced at paced(src) within their lane, so a search adds at most about one request per 2.5 s for a few seconds. That this triggers a 429 is speculative, since it depends on undocumented server limits. No concrete defect is shown.

subsystems.summary: Lines 1236-1572 hold 17 map layers that pull from about 25 public data sources. Most of them follow one template: Layers.add({id, group, name, color, points}), then Points.define(setId, layerId), then a Detail.renderers.<kind> HTML template, then feed(layer, {interval, fetch}). The fetch function calls Net.json, turns the response into plain {lat, lon, r, color, kind, obj, tip} items, calls Points.set, and sets layer.feed.count. The shared canvas, hit-testing, hover, the scheduler and the on/off lifecycle do everything else. That template covers quakes, EONET events, GDACS, storms, news, landing stations, cameras, fires and OSM scan results. The other layers each work their own way. Aurora, RainViewer radar and IR replace enable/disable to manage their own Leaflet overlays. The terminator has no feed and runs its own setInterval. Cables, NWS, events and storms put Leaflet vectors in a group made by lineLayer(). Ships and balloons write into the global Dyn maps, which are drawn by hard-coded branches in Glyphs.draw (lines 649-677). The aisstream WebSocket uses a 30 s feed as a reconnect watchdog. Kp is a separate setInterval that belongs to no layer. The OSM scan builds a fake feed object by hand. Most of the bugs are in lifecycle edge cases: fetches still running when a layer is turned off, stale data that is never removed, and option changes that get dropped. The other two problems are inconsistent HTML escaping in the detail panel templates and one upstream API (RainViewer) that has already changed.

subsystems.extension_points:
How to add a typical point layer (about 15-25 lines). (1) Call `const lyX = Layers.add({ id:'x', group:<one of UI.groups at line 727>, name, desc, color, default:false, points:'x' })`. The group must already be listed in UI.groups. UI.build (line 730) only loops over that list, so a layer with a new group name never shows up in the panel. (2) Call `Points.define('x','x', {minZoom})`. The `points` value in step 1 must equal the set id, or Layers.set will not clear the points when the layer is turned off. (3) Add `Detail.renderers.<kind> = o => \`...\``. The kind string must match the `kind` on each item. If it doesn't, Detail.render does nothing: the panel switches tabs but keeps showing the old content. Every upstream string has to be wrapped in esc() by hand, because Detail.kv values and the Detail.head `sub` argument go in as raw HTML. (4) Add `feed(lyX, { interval, errorInterval, viewDependent, minZoom, fetch: async () => { const d = await Net.json(url); Points.set('x', items); lyX.feed.count = items.length; } })`. Optionally add a friendly hover name in the kindName map at line 813. (5) If the source has no CORS headers, add its host to NEEDS_RELAY (line 483) and to ALLOWED_HOSTS in both serve.js and serve.py. If it needs a key, add an entry to Keys.DEFS (line 1919). (6) If the Brief should use the data, write it into World.* and then edit the Brief code separately.

Point layers are easy to add: the scheduler, error and status UI, hover, selection, zoom gating and world-copy wrapping all come for free. Anything else is harder:
- Moving objects (like ships or balloons) need a new Dyn map and a hand-written branch inside Glyphs.draw (lines 649-677). Nothing there is pluggable, and the existing branches handle the layer on/off check differently from each other.
- Raster or overlay layers need hand-written enable/disable code and an `if (layer.on)` guard after every fetch (copy aurora or rainviewer).
- Vector layers use lineLayer(), which wraps whatever enable/disable exist at the moment it is called, so the order of definitions matters.
- Clickable vector layers also trigger the global map click handler, which opens the probe popup.
- Sub-options added with sub()/UI.pills plus runFeed(feed, true) are silently dropped if a fetch is already running.
- There are no modules, no types and no tests. Many lines are 300-900 characters with several statements each, so diffs and code review are painful. The first refactor I would do is a `layerKit.point({...})` helper plus one escaping templating helper.

Cable landing points (same mirror, then submarinecablemap.com)

subsystems.quality_notes:
Strengths. The point-layer template is good and consistent. About 9 of the 17 layers use exactly Layers.add, Points.define, Detail.renderers, and feed() with Points.set. That gets them scheduling, backoff (errorInterval), status dots and counts, zoom gating, view-dependent refresh, hover, selection and world wrapping with no extra code. The code is defensive in sensible places: isHttp filtering on EONET and GDELT links, both NOAA Kp JSON shapes handled, a fallback URL for cables, per-source and per-district camera caches, bbox gating so multi-MB Caltrans lists load only when on screen, and `if (layer.on)` guards after overlay fetches.

Weaknesses.
- Lifecycle handling is ad hoc. Dyn-backed layers (ships, balloons) aren't gated consistently in the renderer, which causes the ghost-ship and turned-off-balloon bugs, and option changes are lost while a fetch is running.
- HTML escaping is opt-in in each renderer, because Detail.kv and the head sub-line are raw. That is the single most important thing to fix before adding more community or crowd-sourced feeds.
- About 8 of the 17 layers use their own one-off patterns (overlays, lineLayer, Dyn maps, WebSocket, a free-running interval, a fake feed object). Adding another layer of one of those kinds means copying a near neighbour instead of calling a helper.
- Very long multi-statement lines (several over 500 characters) and global mutable state (World, Dyn, auroraOverlay, vesselMeta) make review and refactoring harder. There are no tests.
- At least one upstream source has already broken: RainViewer IR is gone and radar is capped at zoom 7. Many of the 25 sources are unofficial or can change (a personal GitHub cable mirror, data.gov.sg v1, the GDELT DOC API), so expect ongoing maintenance.

Overall the project is a solid base to build on. Before adding many more layers, I would first fix the escaping, the ghost-ship and turned-off-layer bugs, and the dropped option changes. I would also extract a point-layer helper and a moving-object layer helper.

confirmed_issues.description: Detail panel templates put upstream strings into innerHTML without escaping. Detail.kv puts values in as raw HTML (`<dd>${v}</dd>`, line 799), and so does the `sub` argument of Detail.head (line 798). Each renderer has to remember esc(), and several in this range don't. The most exposed case is the balloon 'Heard by' field: SondeHub telemetry is uploaded by anyone with a receiver.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Line 1535: `['Heard by', b.uploader]` takes `uploader: t.uploader_callsign` (line 1539) and inserts it raw through Detail.kv. An uploader callsign such as `` runs script when a user clicks that balloon. The page stores FIRMS, aisstream and Windy keys in localStorage under 'ow.keys' (Keys.get, line 1925), so those keys can be read. Other unescaped spots: EONET `e.cats.join(' · ')` as the sub (1263), GDACS country and severitytext (1283), NHC movement, advisory and sub (1299-1300), Caltrans dir and route (1455), FIRMS acq_date as the sub (1546), and quake status and magType (1246). Detail.links (800) escapes text but never checks isHttp, so camera, GDACS and NHC URLs are not filtered for javascript: links. EONET and GDELT do filter theirs.
confirmed_issues.verification:
Confirmed. Detail.kv inserts values raw (`
${v}
`, line 799) and Detail.head inserts `sub` raw (line 798). Line 1535 passes `b.uploader` (t.uploader_callsign, line 1539) without esc(). SondeHub telemetry is uploaded by the public. Detail.render writes the result to innerHTML (line 796), so an `` payload runs once the user clicks the balloon. The page has no CSP. Keys.get (line 1925) reads the API keys from localStorage 'ow.keys', so injected script on this origin can read them. The other unescaped spots exist as described, but they come from agency feeds (USGS, NASA, GDACS, NHC, Caltrans), which are much less exposed. Detail.links (line 800) does not check isHttp. Medium is fair.

confirmed_issues.description: The primary source for cable and landing data is a personal GitHub repository, and the cable `color` property is put into a style attribute without escaping.
confirmed_issues.evidence: CABLE_URLS[0] and LANDING_URLS[0] (1425-1426) point at raw.githubusercontent.com/lintaojlu/... , which is tried before submarinecablemap.com. Detail.renderers.cable calls `Detail.head(p.color || C.cable, ...)`, which writes `style="background:${color}"` (line 798). A color value such as `red">` in that repo would run when a user clicks a cable.
confirmed_issues.verification: The code behaves as described. CABLE_URLS[0] and LANDING_URLS[0] (lines 1425-1426) point at a personal GitHub repo and are tried first. The cable renderer passes `p.color` into Detail.head, which writes it unescaped into `style="background:${color}"` (line 798). Exploiting this needs the repo owner, or someone who compromises the repo, to plant a payload aimed at this app. That is a supply-chain risk, not one any member of the public can trigger. The same color value only reaches canvas strokeStyle elsewhere, where it is harmless. Real, but low.

confirmed_issues.description: Baltic AIS ships that stop reporting are never removed. Each fetch only adds or overwrites entries in Dyn.ships, so ships stay frozen at their last position for as long as the layer is on.
confirmed_issues.evidence: In the loop at 1509-1510, `if (now - ts > 3600e3) continue;` skips stale vessels but never deletes the `'fi'+mmsi` entry from an earlier fetch. The only cleanup is lyShipsFi.disable (1504), and the 15-minute stale purge at 1529 only touches 'ws' keys. A ship that switches off AIS or leaves coverage stays on the map indefinitely. feed.count (n) counts only fresh ships, so the count shown and the glyphs drawn disagree. Search (2025) also finds these ghost ships.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. The loop at lines 1509-1510 only adds or overwrites `'fi'+mmsi` entries. A vessel whose newest fix is more than 1 h old hits `continue` and keeps its old entry. One that drops out of the response keeps its entry too. The ws purge at line 1529 only removes 'ws' keys, and lyShipsFi.disable (line 1504) only runs on toggle. Ghost ships therefore build up for as long as the layer is on. Glyphs.draw (lines 651 and 662) draws and counts every entry in Dyn.ships, so the cluster count disagrees with feed.count = n (fresh ships only). Search (line 2025) also iterates Dyn.ships and finds them. On a situation map this means showing ships where they no longer are.

confirmed_issues.description: RainViewer's public API has changed. The infrared satellite product was discontinued and personal-use tiles are capped at zoom 7, but the code still requests IR frames and sets radar maxNativeZoom to 12.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Line 1408 reads `d.satellite?.infrared`. RainViewer's transition FAQ says satellite IR data was discontinued, so lyIr will always throw 'no satellite frames' and show a permanent error. Line 1407 sets `maxNativeZoom: 12`, so above zoom 7 Leaflet requests native tiles that are no longer served, and radar disappears or shows placeholder tiles when the user zooms in. Setting maxNativeZoom to 7 would let Leaflet upscale instead.
confirmed_issues.verification: Verified against the live API. weather-maps.json returns `"satellite":{"infrared":[]}`, so line 1408 always throws 'no satellite frames' and the IR layer never works. RainViewer's transition summary lists 'Satellite IR data discontinued' and 'Maximum zoom level set to 7'. With maxNativeZoom: 12 (line 1407), Leaflet requests native tiles at z8-12 that are no longer served, instead of upscaling z7 tiles. Both layers are opt-in (default false), but each is broken when switched on.

confirmed_issues.description: The aisstream handler recounts every ship on every message, and at low zoom it subscribes to the whole world.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Every PositionReport runs `lyShipsWs.feed.count = [...Dyn.ships.keys()].filter(k => k.startsWith('ws')).length`, which is O(N) and allocates two arrays. subscribe() (1524) sends a world-wide box whenever the view spans 360 degrees, with no zoom gate. That means hundreds of messages per second against tens of thousands of ships, so millions of array copies per second on the main thread. Separately, onmessage never calls requestDraw. The 500 ms redraw tick at line 770 only runs when aircraft or satellites exist, so with only ships_ws on, ship positions refresh only when a feed finishes (every 30 s) or the map moves.
confirmed_issues.verification: The main claim holds. Every PositionReport runs `[...Dyn.ships.keys()].filter(k => k.startsWith('ws')).length` (line 1520). That spread-and-filter is O(N) work with allocation on every message. subscribe() (line 1524) widens the box to the whole world when the view spans 360° or crosses the antimeridian, and a low-zoom view covers most of the globe anyway. With tens of thousands of ships in the 15-minute window and a high global message rate, this is a steady main-thread and GC cost. The wording 'millions of array copies per second' is overstated: it is millions of element visits but hundreds of arrays. The redraw sub-claim is also correct but narrow. onmessage never calls requestDraw, and the 500 ms tick (line 770) needs aircraft or satellites present, so this only matters when both are off. Requires an aisstream key, which is opt-in.

confirmed_issues.description: If the balloons layer is turned off while its fetch is still running, the fetch puts balloons back on the map afterwards. Glyphs.draw never checks whether the balloon layer is on.
confirmed_issues.evidence: lyBalloons.disable clears Dyn.balloons (1533). The fetch already in flight (timeout 40 s) then runs `Dyn.balloons.clear(); ... Dyn.balloons.set(...)` (1538-1539), and runFeed's finally block calls requestDraw. The balloon branch at line 667 is `if (Dyn.balloons.size && z >= 4)`, with no Layers.on('balloons') check, so balloons are drawn and clickable while the layer is off. They stay until the layer is toggled on and off again. The same race exists for ships_fi (1506-1510). Its ships are hidden only while ships_ws is also off, because the ship branch at 649 draws every ship whenever either ship layer is on.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. runFeed (lines 777-782) does not re-check d.on after the await. lyBalloons.disable clears Dyn.balloons (line 1533), and the fetch already in flight then repopulates it (lines 1538-1539). requestDraw then runs from line 1540 and from runFeed's finally. The balloon branch at line 667 checks only `Dyn.balloons.size && z >= 4`, with no Layers.on('balloons'), so the balloons are drawn and hit-testable while the layer is off. Nothing clears them until the layer is toggled again. The ships_fi variant is also accurate: line 1510 re-adds the ships, and line 649 draws them whenever ships_ws is on. The window is the length of one fetch, so the impact is low.

confirmed_issues.description: Changing an option (quake feed, news query, camera sources) while that layer's fetch is running is silently dropped. The news detail panel then labels the old results with the new query.
confirmed_issues.evidence: The pill and Run handlers (1243, 1325, 1447) call `runFeed(feed, true)`, which returns immediately if `f.running` (line 777). When the running fetch finishes it sets nextAt to now + interval. A GDELT fetch can take up to 40 s plus a 6 s throttle gap and repeats every 900 s, so a new query can wait 15 minutes. Meanwhile Detail.renderers.news reads `Layers.opt('news_q')` when it renders (1336), so the panel says 'matching <new query>' over results for the old one.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. `if (!d.on || f.running) return;` (line 777) ignores force, so the forced runFeed calls from the pill and Run handlers (lines 1243, 1325, 1447) do nothing while a fetch is in flight. Afterwards nextAt = now + interval (line 780), so a GDELT change waits up to 900 s. A likely trigger is enabling World news and editing the query straight away. The news renderer reads Layers.opt('news_q') at render time (line 1336), so the panel labels old results with the new query. For cameras, map moves shorten the wait because the feed is view-dependent (line 788), but quakes and news really are delayed.

confirmed_issues.description: GDACS from/to dates have no timezone, so they are parsed as local time and then shown with a 'Z' (UTC) suffix.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `fmt.date(p.fromdate)` calls `new Date(t).toISOString()...+'Z'` (line 417). GDACS returns strings like '2026-09-28T12:00:00' with no offset, which ECMAScript parses as local time. A user at UTC-5 sees 17:00Z for a 12:00 UTC event.
confirmed_issues.verification: Verified against the live GDACS API. It returns `"fromdate":"2026-09-13T21:00:00"` with no offset. ECMAScript parses an offset-less date-time as local time. fmt.date (line 417) then prints toISOString() with a 'Z' suffix, so the displayed UTC time is off by the user's UTC offset.

confirmed_issues.description: Clicking an NWS warning polygon shows the alert in the detail panel and also opens a probe popup.
confirmed_issues.evidence: The polygons are interactive canvas paths with the default bubblingMouseEvents. Leaflet fires the path's click (`g.on('click', () => Detail.show('nws', ...))`) and then the map's click handler (line 823). With no glyph under the cursor and cables off, that handler calls `Probe.open(e.latlng)`, which opens a popup and starts weather and geocode requests. The user can never probe inside a warning area without the NWS panel opening too.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. The NWS geoJSON paths (line 1365) are interactive, use vecRenderer, and keep the default Path bubblingMouseEvents: true. The glyph canvas has pointer-events:none (CSS line 117), so the click reaches the vector canvas. In Leaflet 1.9.4, Canvas._onClick calls map._fireDOMEvent with the path as a canvas target. That fires the path's click (propagating to the group handler, which runs Detail.show), then continues to the map. The map's click handler (line 823) finds no glyph and no cable and calls Probe.open, which opens a popup and starts Open-Meteo and Photon requests.

confirmed_issues.description: When an NHC advisory is merged into an existing EONET storm, the data object is updated but its map marker is not.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `dup.kt = dup.kt || s.kt` updates the World.storms object. The canvas item already pushed at line 1310 keeps `color: col` and `tip` computed from EONET's kt, which may be null. A hurricane that EONET lists without a wind magnitude stays blue with no kt in its tooltip, even though NHC reports 64+ kt.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. The canvas item pushed at line 1310 keeps `color: col` and `tip`, both computed from EONET's kt. The NHC merge at line 1316 only mutates the shared object (dup.kt and others), and Points.set at line 1319 reuses the same items. A storm with no EONET kt therefore stays blue and has no kt in its tooltip, while the detail panel shows the NHC kt. Also, `dup.kt || s.kt` prefers an older EONET kt over a newer NHC kt. Low, because EONET usually carries kts.

confirmed_issues.description: Some layers cover only one world copy and others wrap, so behaviour across the 180° meridian is inconsistent.
confirmed_issues.evidence: The aurora imageOverlay is bounded to -180..180 (1382), the terminator polygon spans -180..180 (1415), and cable GeoJSON doesn't wrap either. When the map is centred near 180° (Alaska, Fiji, New Zealand), the eastern half shows no night shading, aurora or cables, while canvas points still wrap through toPt (line 609). FIRMS clamps its bbox with `Math.max(-180, west)` and `Math.min(180, east)` (1549), so fires on the wrapped side are never requested.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Leaflet does not wrap image overlays or vector paths. The aurora overlay bounds are -180..180 (line 1382), the terminator ring spans -180..180 (line 1415), and the cables are plain geoJSON. worldCopyJump keeps the centre within ±180°, but the view can extend past 180, and that part shows no night shading, aurora or cables. Canvas points do wrap via toPt (line 609). FIRMS clamps west and east to ±180 (line 1549), so fires across the antimeridian are never requested. This only matters in the Pacific near 180°.

confirmed_issues.description: OSM scan results are lost if the layer is toggled off and back on.
confirmed_issues.evidence: lyScan has `points:'scan'`, so Layers.set(off) calls Points.clear('scan') (723). Its feed is a hand-built object that is not in Feeds.list (1570), so turning it back on (`feed.nextAt = 0`) refetches nothing. The scan has to be run again from a probe.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Layers.set(off) calls Points.clear('scan') because lyScan has points:'scan' (line 723). The hand-built feed (line 1570) is never added to Feeds.list and its fetch does nothing, so `nextAt = 0` on re-enable restores nothing. Presets that leave out osm_scan (Layers.apply) also wipe the scan. A minor UX loss.

confirmed_issues.description: The Kp poller is outside the feed and layer system, so the Pause button doesn't stop it and its status never appears in the layer list. Its storm warning fires only once per page session.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `fetchKp(); setInterval(fetchKp, 600000);` ignores Feeds.paused (785-786). `window._kpWarned` (1394) is set and never reset, so a second geomagnetic storm days later in a long-running session triggers no log warning.
confirmed_issues.verification: The behaviour is as described. `fetchKp(); setInterval(fetchKp, 600000);` (line 1397) never checks Feeds.paused, although the Setup text at line 1992 says Pause 'stops everything'. window._kpWarned (line 1394) is set once and never reset, so a later storm in the same long session produces no log line. The impact is small: it is one tiny request every 10 minutes, and the chip still turns 'hot' at Kp ≥ 5. Treat as very minor.

confirmed_issues.description: GDELT returns plain-text errors with HTTP 200, and those show up as an unhelpful 'not JSON' error.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Net.json turns a SyntaxError into 'unexpected response (not JSON)' (line 519). GDELT answers bad user queries (short keywords, mixed AND/OR inside the parentheses gdeltQuery adds) and rate limits with a 200 text body. The user sees 'World news: unexpected response (not JSON)' with no clue what is wrong with their query.
confirmed_issues.verification: Partly verified. A malformed query really does return HTTP 200 text/html. I tested the exact form gdeltQuery produces from `(missile OR drone) ukraine`. That form is `((missile OR drone) ukraine)`, and the response was 'Parentheses may only be used around OR'd statements.' with status 200. r.json() then throws a SyntaxError, which line 519 turns into 'unexpected response (not JSON)'. The rate-limit part of the claim is wrong. GDELT returns 429 for rate limiting, and Net.fetch reports it as 'HTTP 429 rate-limited · Please limit…'. gdeltQuery's own re-wrapping (line 1335) can cause the query error.

confirmed_issues.description: The cable click test checks distance to vertices only, not to line segments, and its data is downloaded again every time the layer is turned on.
confirmed_issues.evidence: cableHit compares the click to each `line[i]` vertex only. A click in the middle of a long ocean segment, more than about 10 px from any vertex, falls through to Probe.open. Separately, Layers.set(on) sets `feed.nextAt = 0` (723), so each toggle refetches the multi-MB cable-geo.json even though cableData is still held in memory.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. cableHit (line 1430) measures haversine distance to vertices only. The tolerance is about 10 px of ground distance (roughly 24 km at zoom 6), and ocean segments run far longer between vertices. A mid-segment click misses the cable and falls through to Probe.open. Layers.set(on) sets feed.nextAt = 0 (line 723), and the cable fetch (line 1433) never checks cableData. Net.fetch uses cache:'no-store', so every re-enable downloads the multi-MB GeoJSON again. The landing-point layer behaves the same way.

subsystems.summary: Lines 1573-1748 hold the app's top-level "experience" code. That covers five hard-coded presets ("views") and the legend; geolocation through navigator.geolocation with an ipapi.co IP fallback; the FUN helpers ("Surprise me" military pick, ISS follow, and a nearest-camera finder that nothing calls); the Brief, a live situation summary; and the first-run Welcome dialog. Brief.render (1640-1713) is one large function. Every 5 s it reads globals (Dyn.air, Dyn.sats, World.*, Space, Aurora, AirSweep and the ly* feed objects), builds HTML for each section (emergencies, military air, degraded GPS, ISS/space, hazards, Kp/aurora, records with a canvas sparkline, news) and replaces #brief's innerHTML. Clicks are handled by one delegated listener (2041) that sends "kind:value" strings to Brief.act. Presets work by calling Layers.apply(list of layer ids) and overwriting the persisted sat_groups option, then either flying to a fixed view or calling Locate.go / Fun.followIss. The code works and escapes its HTML carefully: every dynamic string goes through esc(), and I found no XSS. It does have several real logic bugs: ISS follow/preset interaction, stale hazard data, wrong ISS-visibility and aurora math, and pass-countdown caching.

Optionally add sats (CelesTrak group ids from Sats.GROUPS, 1103) and either view: [lat, lon, zoom] or go. The #views rail and the Welcome grid are generated from PRESETS automatically.
