subsystems.quality_notes:
Strengths:
- HTML escaping is consistent: esc() is applied to every feed-derived string, and data-act values are escaped and read back through dataset.
- The Brief's ideas are good: emergency squawks, a military role breakdown, GNSS-interference clustering, ISS passes, records.
- Adding a preset or legend entry is a one-line data change.
- Calls into other modules (Layers, Sats, Air, Detail, Tracks) go through clear method names.

Weaknesses for extending:
- Brief.render is a single ~70-line function built from very long one-line template expressions with nested ternaries. It has no per-section error isolation, so one throw blanks the whole Brief, and the 5 s interval's errors go only to the console (window.onerror at 2078 filters to satellite/Leaflet messages).
- The Brief reads globals directly (World.*, Dyn, Space, Aurora, AirSweep, lyAirEmg/lyAirMil/lyQuakes/lyStorms). This works only because of script order, and because World data outlives its layer, every section has to remember to check Layers.on.
- Action dispatch ('kind:value' strings in Brief.act), preset 'go' handling, and layer ids in PRESETS are unchecked magic strings, so typos fail silently.
- State resets are ad hoc: `Sel.kind = null` instead of Detail.clear(), issFollow cleared only on dragstart, Presets.current stays highlighted after manual layer changes.
- Some constants are duplicated: LEGEND hard-codes '#ff9ad5' and '#7fd0ff', which also appear in the renderer and the storm layer.
- The sparkline canvas ignores devicePixelRatio, so it is blurry on HiDPI screens.

Treat the range as a working prototype. Before adding many more Brief sections, the first refactors should be: a section registry with try/catch, a clear-on-disable rule for World data, and a single 'follow' state machine shared with Air.follow.

confirmed_issues.description: The 'Space' preset's ISS follow is undone or never starts. Presets.apply runs Fun.followIss and then immediately clears the selection and ground track it just made. If the ISS is not loaded yet, followIss does nothing and its hint toast is overwritten.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Line 1587 calls Fun.followIss(), which calls Detail.show('sat', iss) and Sats.drawTrack(iss); drawTrack puts the track and footprint into Tracks.group (1183-1184). Line 1588 then runs `Sel.kind = null; Tracks.clear(); toast(`View: ${p.name}`)`. Case A, ISS loaded: the track and footprint are wiped at once, and with Sel.kind null the auto re-draw at 1165 (`Sel.kind === 'sat'`) never fires. The detail tab is left showing a frozen ISS panel, because the 2 s refresh at 802 needs Sel.kind. Case B, sats off or still loading (lySats.disable empties byId at 1233): Sats.iss() is null, followIss toasts 'Loading the ISS orbit… try again in a moment' and returns, and line 1588's toast replaces that text in the same tick. The user picks 'Space' and is never told to retry. Also, Sel.obj is not cleared, so a previously selected point-layer object stays highlighted (renderer check `Sel.obj === it.obj` at 619).
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed, though partly overstated. Line 1587 calls Fun.followIss(), which sets Sel.kind='sat' through Detail.show (794) and draws the track into Tracks.group (1183-1184). Line 1588 then runs Sel.kind=null and Tracks.clear() in the same tick, so the track and footprint vanish. Because Sel.kind is null, neither the 1165 auto-redraw nor the 2 s detail refresh at 802 runs, and the detail panel freezes. The pan-follow itself (issFollow=true) does survive when the ISS is loaded. Case B is common and fully real: going from Hazards (sats off, so lySats.disable at 1233 empties byId) to Space leaves Sats.iss() null. followIss returns without flying anywhere, and toast() (451) is a single element, so 'View: Space' overwrites the 'try again' hint at once. Sel.obj is not cleared, and the canvas highlight check at 619 does not look at Sel.kind.

confirmed_issues.description: ISS follow is only cancelled by a mouse/touch drag. It keeps panning back to the ISS and interrupts every programmatic flyTo (presets, Brief items, Surprise me, Locate, search). It also fights Air.follow.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `map.on('dragstart', () => { Fun.issFollow = false; })` (1631) is the only reset. The interval at 1632 calls map.panTo(ISS) every 2.5 s, and Leaflet's setView/panTo stops any running flyTo. Scenario: press 'i', then click a military item in the Brief (Brief.act 'air' does a flyTo, 1724). Within 2.5 s the map is pulled back to the ISS. Keyboard arrow panning and Escape (Detail.clear, 2069) do not stop it either. If the user also clicks Follow on an aircraft (Air.following, panned every 3 s at 931), the map alternates between the aircraft and the ISS. If sats are turned off and back on later (e.g. preset 4 then preset 1), the stale issFollow=true flag resumes jumping to the ISS without being asked.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. The dragstart handler at 1631 is the only place that resets Fun.issFollow; Escape and Detail.clear (2069, 795) do not touch it. The 2.5 s interval at 1632 calls map.panTo, which goes through Leaflet setView, and setView calls _stop(), cancelling any flyTo in flight. So a Brief act, preset, Surprise or Locate flyTo is aborted or pulled back to the ISS within 2.5 s. Air.following (931, every 3 s) has the same dragstart-only reset (933), so the map alternates between the aircraft and the ISS. If sats are turned off, byId is emptied and Sats.iss() returns null, but the flag stays set, so following resumes after sats reload.

confirmed_issues.description: The Hazards and World news sections keep showing data for layers that are switched off. World.* arrays are never cleared, so the Brief shows frozen quakes, storms, GDACS alerts, tornado warnings and news indefinitely.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Layers.set(id,false) (723) only calls d.disable and Points.clear. Nothing resets World.quakes / storms / gdacs / nws / news (filled at 1249, 1303, 1287, 1362, 1349). Brief.render shows them without checking the layer: `if (q.length)` (1686), `if (World.storms.length)` (1688), `red.length` (1690), `tor.length` (1691), `if (World.news.length)` (1709). Scenario: apply 'Storms & quakes', then 'Military air picture' (which turns off quakes/events/gdacs/storms/nws/radar). The Brief keeps listing the M-largest quake, Red/Orange GDACS alerts and tornado warnings from the moment the layers were turned off, with no further updates, and clicking them opens details for points not drawn on the map. Aurora.grid (1696) has the same problem once the aurora layer is off.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Layers.set(off) (723) calls only d.disable, Points.clear and a feed status reset. None of the disables for quakes, events, gdacs, storms, nws or news (lineLayer at 1238, and lyAurora.disable at 1374 for Aurora.grid) clear the World.* arrays, which are only reassigned inside the fetches (1249, 1287, 1303, 1349, 1362). Brief.render checks only array length at 1686, 1688, 1690, 1691 and 1709, with no Layers.on gate. The 'Military air picture' preset therefore leaves frozen quakes, GDACS alerts and 'N tornado warnings active in the US' on screen indefinitely, and Brief.act 'quake' or 'storm' opens details for points that are no longer drawn.

confirmed_issues.description: The 'sunlit in a dark sky: go look' hint tests whether the sun is above the horizon at the ISS's sub-point. The ISS at about 420 km stays sunlit until the sub-point sun elevation drops to roughly -20°. So the hint almost never appears for the classic visible pass.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `sunElevation(pos.lat, pos.lon, now) < -6 && sunElevation(iss.lat, iss.lon, now) > 0`. When the ISS is high in the observer's sky, its sub-point is a few hundred km away and has nearly the observer's sun elevation. Example: observer at 40N with the sun at -12°, ISS at 60° elevation. Sub-point sun elevation is about -11°, the condition is false, and nothing is shown, even though the ISS is brightly sunlit (shadow limit about -acos(6371/(6371+alt)) ≈ -20°). The hint can only fire when the ISS is low toward the twilight glow.
confirmed_issues.verification: Physics is correct. At about 420 km the ISS stays illuminated until the sun is about acos(6371/6791) ≈ 20° below the horizon at its sub-point. The condition at 1675 requires sunElevation at the sub-point > 0. For a high pass the sub-point lies within a few hundred km of an observer whose sun is below -6°, so the condition is false. The hint fires only for low passes toward the twilight side. It affects only an optional hint text, so the severity is low.

confirmed_issues.description: The ISS pass cache (5 min) shows a negative countdown, 'Next pass over you in -4 min', for several minutes after almost every pass.
confirmed_issues.evidence: issPass.v is recomputed only when the key changes or after 300 s (1673). Sats.nextPass starts at Date.now() and returns the pass in progress with start≈now (1203). After the ISS sets (el ≤ 0 at 1674-1675), line 1676 renders `fmt.mins((p.start - now) / 60000)` from the cached, already-finished pass. fmt.mins(-4) gives '-4 min'. This lasts until the next 5-min refresh. The cache is never invalidated when p.end < now.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. If the 5-min cache (1673) is refreshed while el ≥ 10°, nextPass (1200-1204) starts at Date.now() and returns start≈now for the pass in progress. Once the ISS drops below 0°, line 1676 renders (p.start - now)/60000, which is negative. fmt.mins (418) gives '-N min' for negative values because they are < 60. This persists until the cache is 300 s old. Nothing invalidates the cache when p.end < now. It needs the Brief tab open and a position set, and happens after many passes but not all.

confirmed_issues.description: The aurora visibility verdict compares the user's geographic latitude against an oval latitude that the text itself calls geomagnetic. The answer can be off by up to about 10° depending on longitude.
confirmed_issues.evidence: k.lat = 66.5 - 2.05*Kp is labelled 'geomagnetic latitude', but the test is `Math.abs(pos.lat) >= k.lat - 5` using geographic pos.lat. Kp 6: threshold 49.2°. Minneapolis (geographic 45°N, geomagnetic ≈55°) is told 'too far from the poles right now' during a storm that is typically visible there. Kp 4: threshold 53.3°. Moscow (geographic 55.8°N, geomagnetic ≈51°) is told 'possible on your horizon tonight'. It also says 'tonight' in daylight. When the OVATION value is present it can contradict the verdict in the same sentence.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. kpText (1639) gives a geomagnetic-latitude boundary and the label says 'geomagnetic latitude', but line 1696 compares it to Math.abs(pos.lat), which is geographic. In North America geomagnetic latitude is about 9-10° higher than geographic, and in Russia and East Asia it is lower, so the verdict is systematically biased by region. 'Tonight' is printed regardless of daylight. It is an advisory heuristic shown next to the OVATION percentage, so the severity is low.

confirmed_issues.description: A preset's satellite groups can be silently dropped for up to 2 hours if a satellite reload is already running. Sats.reload() returns early while loading, and the feed only re-checks every 7200 s.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Presets.apply does `Layers.setOpt('sat_groups', p.sats); if (lySats.on) Sats.reload();`. Sats.reload begins with `if (this.loading) return;` (1130), and the running reload captured groupsOn() before the change (1132). The sats feed interval is 7200 s (1235), so the stale-group check doesn't run again for 2 h. This is the first-run path: the splash closes, Welcome opens while CelesTrak TLEs are still downloading (2 s gap, up to 90 s timeout), and the user clicks 'Space'. GPS ('gps-ops') never loads. Fun.followIss (1619) has the same pattern for adding 'stations'.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Sats.reload returns at once while loading (1130). The in-flight reload read groupsOn() before its first await (1132), so it uses the old groups. The feed then schedules nextAt = now + 7200 s (780, 1235), and the stale-group check only runs then. On first run, uncached TLEs (90 s timeout, 2 s gap) can still be loading when Welcome appears (2056), so choosing Space drops 'gps-ops' for up to 2 h. followIss at 1619 has the same pattern. It needs a timing overlap, so the severity is low.

confirmed_issues.description: Presets and followIss overwrite saved options (sat_groups, sat_tracks) but never re-render the Satellites sub-row pills. The layer panel then shows the wrong groups and the user's own selection is lost.
confirmed_issues.evidence: The pills are built once in lySats.sub (1229-1231) by UI.pills (762), which sets the 'on' class at build time. UI.build runs only at init (2039). Scenario: the user enabled Starlink, then picks 'Around me' (sats: ['stations']). Starlink is removed from sat_groups, but its pill still shows 'on'. The first click on it sends setOn(false), a no-op, and flips the pill. followIss's `Layers.setOpt('sat_tracks', true)` (1620) likewise leaves the 'auto ground track' pill showing off.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. UI.pills (762) sets the 'on' class only at build time, and UI.build runs only at init (2039). Presets.apply (1585) and followIss (1619-1620) change sat_groups and sat_tracks through setOpt without re-rendering the pills. A pill left showing 'on' for a removed group sends setOn(id, false) on the first click, which changes nothing but triggers a reload and flips the pill. It takes two clicks to actually re-add the group.

confirmed_issues.description: Every 5 s the Brief replaces its whole innerHTML. Keyboard focus is lost and clicks that span a re-render are dropped.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `this.el.innerHTML = parts.join('')` runs from the 5 s interval at 1733 whenever the Brief tab is on. A keyboard user who Tabs to a Brief item has focus reset to <body> within 5 s. A mousedown on an .item button just before the tick and a mouseup just after land on different elements, so no click event fires and Brief.act never runs. Text selection is also wiped.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Line 1711 replaces this.el.innerHTML every 5 s through the interval at 1733 whenever the Brief tab is on. A focused .item button is destroyed, so focus falls back to body. Clicks are handled by delegation at 2041 with e.target.closest('[data-act]'). If the mousedown target is removed before mouseup, the click either is not fired or fires on a common ancestor with no data-act, so Brief.act does not run. The window is small (press duration out of 5 s), but the keyboard focus loss is deterministic.

confirmed_issues.description: 'Shown once' is not true when the Welcome dialog is dismissed with Escape. The skip link also cannot be reached from the keyboard.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Only the preset buttons and #wSkip call done(), which runs Store.set('welcomed', true). The global Escape handler (2069) only sets `$('#welcome').hidden = true`, so Splash.close (2056) shows the Welcome again on every launch. 'Just show the map' is `<a id="wSkip">` with no href (1743), so it is not in the tab order. Pressing 1-5 while the Welcome is open applies a preset but leaves the modal covering the map.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Escape at 2069 only sets #welcome.hidden=true. It never calls Store.set('welcomed', true), which happens only in done() (1744), so Splash.close (2056) shows the Welcome again on the next launch, contradicting 'Shown once'. <a id="wSkip"> has no href (1743), so it is not in the tab order. Keys 1-5 call Presets.apply (2070) but leave the full-screen #welcome overlay (287, z-index 1500) up. Keyboard users can still dismiss it through the focusable preset buttons or Escape, so the severity is low.

confirmed_issues.description: If the user denies the browser location prompt, the app still geolocates them through a third-party IP service and saves the result. The saved position is then used indefinitely, and an unanswered prompt leaves 'Center on me' hanging with no feedback.
confirmed_issues.evidence: The geolocation error callback is `ip`, which calls Net.json('https://ipapi.co/json/') and Store.set('pos') (1601-1602), with no distinction for PERMISSION_DENIED. Brief.render reads Locate.pos with no age check (1642), so ISS passes, aurora and 'nearest you' keep using a position days old after the laptop moves. The {timeout: 8000} option does not run while the permission prompt is open, so if the user ignores the prompt the Promise in Locate.go (1606) never settles.
confirmed_issues.verification: Narrowly real. The getCurrentPosition error callback at 1603 is ip() for every error code, PERMISSION_DENIED included. A user who blocks location on 'Center on me' is still located by an ipapi.co lookup, and the result is persisted with Store.set at 1601. The toast does say 'approximate (IP)', and the user did start the action, so this is a privacy-expectation issue, not a security vulnerability. The stale-position and hanging-prompt sub-claims are weaker: a saved location is a reasonable design, and the browser prompt itself is the visible feedback.

confirmed_issues.description: Dead code: Fun.nearestCam and Locate.get are never called. Locate.go always re-prompts or re-queries instead of using the 6 h cache that get() implements.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Searching the file finds no reference to nearestCam outside its definition (1623) and no Locate.get( call; the callers are 1587, 1730 and 2040, which all use Locate.go → refresh(). nearestCam also ignores the user's cam_src filter, so wiring it up as-is could fly to a disabled camera network.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed by grep. nearestCam appears only at its definition (1623), and Locate.get( has no callers; they are reachable only through the window.OW console handle (2082). This is dead code, a minor maintainability point. Locate.go skipping the 6 h cache is defensible for an explicit 'Center on me' refresh, so only the dead-code part stands.

rejected_issues.description: Degraded-GPS clustering uses a fixed 4° grid. One jamming area is split into several 'top 3' rows, which can push a separate hotspot out of the list.
rejected_issues.reason: The arithmetic is described correctly: Math.round(lat/4)*4 puts cell boundaries at 2° offsets, so a large interference area spans several cells. That is the inherent tradeoff of a coarse fixed-grid heuristic, not a defect, and each row is a factually correct count. regionOf (440) would also label neighbouring cells differently ('the Baltic', 'the Baltic states', 'Poland'), not three identical rows. The text at 1664 never claims a worldwide count, so the headline sub-claim is not a defect either. Better clustering would be an enhancement, not a bug fix.

subsystems.summary: Lines 1749-1916 hold the audio subsystem, split into three objects. Synth is a generative WebAudio sequencer. Each start builds a long-lived graph: a 2 s pink-noise buffer, a static bed with an LFO, 3 pad oscillators, 2 drone oscillators, a lowpass and a feedback delay. A 40 ms setInterval then schedules short-lived drum/bass/blip voices 180 ms ahead, which is the standard look-ahead pattern. Three presets (SETS) set tempo, drums, hats, arp and filter cutoff. Radio fetches up to 14 stations per genre tag from radio-browser.info, trying five hard-coded mirrors one after another and caching results in memory for an hour. Note that there is no SomaFM code anywhere in the file. Music is the controller: it lazily creates one AudioContext (master gain, analyser, destination), plays radio through a plain HTMLAudioElement that is not routed through Web Audio, persists mode/set/volume/station to localStorage, rebuilds the popover HTML, and runs a requestAnimationFrame visualizer. The visualizer reads the analyser for the synth but only draws a fake sine animation for radio. The autoplay policy is respected: every Music.start path comes from a click or keydown (splash button at 2056, keys at 2070, popover), and ensure() creates the context synchronously before the first await. The main weaknesses are in the async start/busy handling and in node and loop lifecycle.

key_functions.role: Glides pad and drone oscillators to the next chord in PROG (every 8 bars)

key_functions.role: Look-ahead loop: schedules every 16th whose time is before currentTime+0.18 s

key_functions.name: Synth.play
key_functions.role: Per-16th pattern logic: kick/snare/hat/bass/blip decisions driven by set flags and the density/brightness inputs

key_functions.name: Music.start

key_functions.role: Rebuilds the whole popover via innerHTML (modes, sets or tags+stations, volume, autostart) and re-binds all handlers

subsystems.extension_points:
New generated set: add an entry to Synth.SETS (name, desc, bpm, drums, half, hats, arp, cut). The popover list (Object.entries at 1887) and the 'n' key cycle (Object.keys at 2070) pick it up automatically. Anything rhythmically new, though, means editing the hard-coded branches in Synth.play (1806-1814), which only know 'half-time' and 'four-on-the-floor'. PROG and PENTA are global, not per set. Moving kick/snare/bass step patterns and the progression into the set objects would make sets data-only. Never rename or remove an existing set id without migrating localStorage (see the music_set issue).

New radio genre: append to Radio.TAGS.

New radio provider (e.g. SomaFM, which the brief mentions but which does not exist in the code): playback itself is provider-agnostic, because Music.setStation({name,url}) plays any http(s) stream through startRadio. Radio.list and the radio branch of renderPop, however, are radio-browser-specific. You would add a provider abstraction ({id, label, list(tag) -> [{id,name,url,codec,bitrate,country,tags}]}) plus a provider selector in renderPop.

New map-reactive behavior: put the computation in Music.react (1874) as another Synth field and read it in Synth.play.

What makes extension hard:
(1) Music has no explicit state machine. start() awaits and then re-reads this.mode/this.station, and the busy flag silently drops requests, so every new control adds race surface.
(2) renderPop rebuilds the entire popover on every ui() call, including each buffering event, so any new widget in the popover (e.g. a slider) gets destroyed mid-interaction.
(3) Radio bypasses Web Audio. A real radio visualizer, master-bus volume, ducking under alert pings, or effects would need createMediaElementSource. That needs crossOrigin='anonymous' plus CORS headers on the stream (most stations have none, and without them the source outputs silence), or streaming through the local /proxy, which is an allowlist and is not built for endless responses.
(4) The page served over https (rather than the http://127.0.0.1 helper) would hit mixed-content blocking or auto-upgrade for the many http:// station URLs.

data_sources.name: radio-browser.info station directory (mirrors de1, nl1, at1, de2, fi1; /json/stations/bytag/{tag}?limit=14&hidebroken=true&order=clickcount&reverse=true)
Third-party broadcaster audio streams (url_resolved from the directory, played via HTMLAudioElement)

subsystems.quality_notes:
Strong parts:
- The synth design is reasonable and cheap: about 8 continuous nodes, plus roughly 10-25 short-lived self-stopping voice nodes per second, scheduled with the standard look-ahead (40 ms timer, 180 ms horizon) on the audio clock. CPU cost is low, and the synth keeps playing in a background tab because audible tabs are not timer-throttled.
- Autoplay handling is correct by construction: the splash 'enter with audio' button is the gate, and ensure() runs synchronously inside the gesture before any await.
- Station data is handled defensively: names go through esc(), only http(s) URLs are accepted (1835, 1842), and homepage is stored but never rendered as a link.

Weak parts:
- The async controller relies on a single busy flag. It drops requests silently and re-reads mutable state after an await.
- Several lifecycles are tied to the 'playing' boolean being observed on a later frame: the vis loop, and fail() closures that act on elements that are no longer current.
- `audio.src = ''` in stop (1859) fires an 'error' event by spec, which reaches the old element's fail() and clears radioState. That is harmless today but is a trap; prefer removeAttribute('src') followed by load().
- The radio volume slider sets HTMLMediaElement.volume, which iOS Safari ignores.
- The code is dense one-line methods with magic numbers inline, which makes the races above hard to see.

Before building more on this area, it is worth introducing:
- a small explicit state machine (idle / connecting / playing / error) with a connect timeout and an AbortController-style token, so stale completions are ignored;
- a single vis loop started once;
- validation of persisted ids;
- full disconnect in Synth.stop;
- a targeted UI update path instead of rebuilding the popover via innerHTML.

confirmed_issues.description: State that changes while Music.start is awaiting a radio connection is never reconciled. The result is synth and radio playing together, or the UI showing and saving a different station from the one actually playing.
confirmed_issues.evidence: start() sets busy=true, then `await this.startRadio()` (1853), then re-reads `if (this.mode === 'synth') { ... Synth.start(...) }` (1854). Case 1: in radio mode, click a station that takes a few seconds to connect, and during 'connecting...' click 'Generated' (1891: sets mode='synth'; playing is false so nothing stops) or press 'n' (setSet, 1871). When the stream connects, the radio Audio element plays AND Synth.start runs; the label shows the synth set name. Case 2: click station A, then station B while A is connecting. setStation (1872) stores B in this.station and localStorage, but start() returns immediately because busy is true. A then connects; 1855 logs `Radio: B`, and label() (1877) shows B's name while A's stream plays. B is persisted as the saved station.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. The mode check at 1853 runs before `await this.startRadio()`, and 1854 reads `this.mode` again after the await. If the user clicks 'Generated' during 'connecting…', 1891 sets mode='synth' (playing is false, so nothing stops), startRadio later resolves and Synth.start runs while the Audio element also plays. Case 2 is also real. setStation (1872) overwrites this.station and the stored station, then start() returns because busy is true. Station A plays, while 1855 and label() (1877) report B. Downgraded from high: the user has to act during the connect window, the map is unaffected, and Stop clears both (stop() pauses this.audio and calls Synth.stop).

confirmed_issues.description: There is no timeout or cancel for a radio connection, so a stream that never answers leaves Music.busy true and blocks every audio control.
confirmed_issues.evidence: startRadio resolves or rejects only on a.play()'s promise or the 'error' event (1865-1867). A server that accepts the TCP connection but never sends data leaves play() pending: no 'error' fires, only 'stalled'/'waiting'. While pending, busy=true (1850), so the Stop/Play button (toggle -> start, 1860), setSet's restart and the 'Generated' set buttons (1892 `if (!this.playing) this.start()`) all return without doing anything. The label stays 'connecting...' until the browser's network stack gives up, possibly minutes later. stop() cannot cancel either, because it returns early when !playing (1859).
confirmed_issues.verification: The code matches the report. startRadio (1861-1868) has no timeout, and busy stays true until play() settles. While pending, toggle->start (1850) and the 1892 start return immediately, and stop() (1859) returns because playing is false, so nothing can cancel the connection. Retired, refused or geo-blocked streams fire 'error' or a TCP timeout and recover. Only a server that accepts the connection and then sends nothing keeps play() pending indefinitely. That is uncommon, so the severity is low.

confirmed_issues.description: When a stream fails or ends after it has started, the app keeps showing radio as playing although it is silent, and gives no message.
confirmed_issues.evidence: The 'error' listener is `{ once: true }` and calls fail(), which clears radioState, nulls this.audio and calls reject() on a promise that has already resolved (a no-op). It never sets playing=false, calls ui() or shows a toast. 'ended' (an Icecast server closing the connection) is not handled at all. A Wi-Fi blip that kills the stream therefore leaves #btnAudio 'on' and the HUD showing '▶ Station name', with no sound. The user has to click Stop and then Play to recover.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. After play() has resolved, fail() (1864) clears radioState and this.audio and calls reject() on an already-settled promise. It never sets playing=false, never calls ui() and shows no toast. 'ended' has no listener. #btnAudio and #hudAudio keep showing the station as playing, or a stale 'buffering…', while nothing plays, and the radio visualizer (1911) keeps animating. Internet radio drops are common, and only Stop then Play recovers.

confirmed_issues.description: Synth.start sets live=true before building the graph, and Music.set is loaded from localStorage without validation. A stale or renamed set id therefore leaves the soundtrack broken for the rest of the session.
confirmed_issues.evidence: 1840: `set: Store.get('music_set', 'underground')` is not checked against Synth.SETS (unlike the station, which 1842 validates). If a future build renames or removes a set, a returning user's start() calls Synth.start. That sets `this.live = true` (1762), then throws a TypeError at 1770 (`this.SETS[this.set].cut`) after creating only noise/bus/lp. Music.start catches it and shows 'Audio failed to start'. Synth.live is now stuck true with a half-built this.n. Every later Synth.start returns early, and setSet/Music.start call Synth.use (1791), which dereferences `this.n.delay.delayTime` -> TypeError again. Audio is dead until reload.
confirmed_issues.verification: The cascade is accurate. 1762 sets live=true before 1770 dereferences SETS[this.set].cut. After the throw, live stays true with n.lp built and n.delay missing, so later Synth.use (1791) throws on n.delay, including from setSet and the 'n' key. Today every stored value comes from Synth.SETS keys (1892, and 2070 cycles a valid key), so the bug is latent. It only triggers if a future build renames or removes a set, or if storage is hand-edited. The station validation at 1842 shows this project has already had a stored-schema change. Low because nothing triggers it today.

confirmed_issues.description: Clicking the already-active 'Generated' mode button while it plays rebuilds the whole synth graph and adds another requestAnimationFrame loop each time, with no upper limit.
confirmed_issues.evidence: The mode handler does `if (this.playing) { this.stop(); if (this.mode === 'synth' || this.station) this.start(); }` without checking that the mode changed. In synth mode, start() runs synchronously (no await when the context is already running), so playing goes false -> true within one task. The previous vis() loop (1906-1908, which exits only when it sees !playing on a frame) never sees false and keeps running, while 1855 calls vis() again. N clicks give N+1 loops, each doing getComputedStyle (via cssVar), getByteFrequencyData and 18 fillRects per frame until the next real stop. Each click also audibly restarts the beat and builds a fresh noise buffer and 5 oscillators. The same synchronous double start happens on radio->synth via setSet (1871). The unused setMode (1870) would do it on every call if it were wired up.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. 1891 restarts without checking that the mode changed. Once the AudioContext is running, start() in synth mode never reaches an await, so playing goes false->true in the same task. The old vis() frame (1907) never sees !playing, and 1855 starts another loop. The same happens with the 'n' key from radio mode through setSet (2070/1871). The extra loops end at the next real stop, and each costs one analyser read and 18 fillRects per frame. The visible effects are an audible beat restart and some wasted CPU, not a medium performance problem.

confirmed_issues.description: toggle() saves music_auto=false whenever start() has not finished synchronously. In radio mode, pressing Play turns 'start with the page' off.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `if (this.playing) this.stop(); else this.start(); Store.set('music_auto', this.auto = this.playing);`. start() is async, and in radio mode playing becomes true only after `await this.startRadio()`. So the ▶ Play button (1890) or the 'a' key stores auto=false. The re-rendered popover then shows the 'start with the page' box unchecked, and on the next visit the splash defaults to 'silent' (2059). The same happens when toggle is pressed while busy.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. toggle() (1860) reads this.playing synchronously after calling async start(). In radio mode, playing only becomes true after `await this.startRadio()`, so the Play button (1890) or the 'a' key (2070) stores music_auto=false. The next renderPop shows the box unchecked, and 2059 then makes 'silent' the default splash button. The effect is cosmetic or preference-only, since the splash does not auto-start audio.

confirmed_issues.description: Every ui() call rebuilds the whole popover. This includes the radio element's 'waiting'/'playing' events, which destroys controls mid-interaction and re-queries the directory when it is down.
confirmed_issues.evidence: 1866: the 'waiting'/'playing' listeners call this.ui(), and 1880 calls renderPop() whenever the popover is open. renderPop replaces pop.innerHTML (1885), so a volume slider being dragged is removed from the DOM during a rebuffer and the drag ends. In radio mode each rebuild calls Radio.list (1897). Failures are not cached (1834 caches successes only), so on a flaky stream with the directory unreachable, every buffering event fires another series of up to 5 mirror requests with a 12 s timeout each.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. The 'waiting'/'playing' listeners (1866) call ui(), and ui() calls renderPop (1880) when the popover is open. renderPop rewrites innerHTML (1885), which detaches a slider that is being dragged or a station button between mousedown and mouseup, and resets the list's scroll position. The comment at 2062 shows the author knows re-renders detach elements. Radio.list caches only successes (1834-1835), so with the directory down, every rebuild starts another run of up to 5 mirror requests. The isConnected guards (1897/1900) prevent stale writes, so the harm is wasted requests and annoying UI behavior.

confirmed_issues.description: Synth.stop disconnects only bus, bedG and wet. The lowpass stays connected to master and the delay/feedback cycle stays wired, so each start/stop cycle leaves a few nodes attached to the live graph.
confirmed_issues.evidence: stop's cleanup calls `n.bus.disconnect(); n.bedG.disconnect(); n.wet.disconnect();`. n.lp's outputs (to `out` and n.delay, set up at 1773) and the n.delay->n.fb->n.delay loop (1772) are never disconnected. Because the old n.lp still feeds Music.master, the master node keeps references to every old filter, so stop/start cycles (toggle, set changes, mode switches) slowly grow the graph. Each leftover node is silent and cheap, but it is never freed.
confirmed_issues.verification: Partly accurate. stop() (1789) disconnects only bus, bedG and wet. lp->out, lp->delay and the delay<->fb cycle (1772-1773) stay wired. Whether master keeps the old lp alive depends on the implementation. A DelayNode feedback cycle where each node has an incoming connection from the other is the textbook case of a Web Audio node leak, though. So each start/stop cycle (toggle, mode or set change, and the restart from issue 5) can leave a few silent nodes behind. Real but minor.

confirmed_issues.description: Once created, the AudioContext is never suspended. It keeps rendering silence through master->analyser->destination after Stop and during radio mode. Music.ensure also orphans any context that Sound created earlier.
confirmed_issues.evidence: There is no ctx.suspend() or ctx.close() in the file (grep). stop() (1859) only stops the synth and the radio element, so the audio render thread keeps waking every 128-frame quantum and holds the output device open (matters on battery). In radio mode the analyser is fed nothing, since the HTMLAudioElement is not routed into the context. 1847 `Sound.ctx = ctx` replaces any AudioContext that Sound.ping (458) already created, e.g. at init via Sound.toggle(Sound.on) at 2039 when alerts were left on. That earlier context is never closed.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed by grep: there is no suspend() or close() on either AudioContext. After stop(), Music.ctx keeps rendering silence through master->analyser->destination, and in radio mode the analyser receives nothing because the Audio element is not routed into the context. 1847 overwrites Sound.ctx. If alerts were on, init (2039 -> 454 -> 458) had already created a context, and that one is orphaned and never closed. This leaks one context and keeps the audio device open, which costs some power but does not grow over time.

confirmed_issues.description: 'Traffic density' is measured from the total aircraft count, not the aircraft in view, so it pins at 1 whenever a large feed is on.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `const inView = Dyn.air.size; Synth.density = Math.min(1, inView / 900);`. Dyn.air (580) holds every tracked aircraft worldwide (military worldwide, OpenSky global snapshot at 1056). With OpenSky enabled (thousands of records) the hat density is always at maximum regardless of where the map is. The comment and variable name promise a viewport-based measure.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. 1875 uses Dyn.air.size, and Dyn.air (580) holds every tracked aircraft. OpenSky's global snapshot (1052-1056) inserts thousands, and military-worldwide adds hundreds wherever the map is. Synth.density therefore stays at 1 with OpenSky on and ignores panning, despite the name inView and the 'listens to the map' comment. The only effect is the hi-hat probability (1805), which is cosmetic.

rejected_issues.description: The look-ahead scheduler never re-syncs. After any main-thread stall longer than about 140 ms, it schedules every missed 16th at a time already in the past, and they all sound at once.
rejected_issues.reason: The missing re-sync is real, but the claimed 'audible pile-up' does not happen. Every percussive voice uses env() (1816), whose exponential ramps decay to .0001 at t+a+d. An event scheduled with t well in the past is evaluated near its end value, so it is essentially silent. A kick 300 ms late is about -70 dB, and a bass tail is similar. Oscillator stop() times in the past stop the voice immediately. What the user hears is the same gap a re-sync would leave, plus at most one attenuated tail. In the throttled-tab case the voices are created and stopped at once and are silent. That is a brief CPU burst, not an audible defect.

rejected_issues.description: The visualizer calls getComputedStyle on the document root every animation frame.
rejected_issues.reason: --vibe is defined once at :root (line 21) and never changed at runtime, so caching it would be safe. The cost claim is weak, though. getComputedStyle().getPropertyValue only recalculates style that is already dirty, and the browser would recalculate it before painting that frame anyway. Canvas drawing in the same frame does not dirty style. The extra work is negligible, which makes this a micro-optimization nit rather than a defect.

rejected_issues.description: The station directory uses a hard-coded list of radio-browser mirrors tried one after another, with a 12 s timeout each.
rejected_issues.reason: The loop at 1835 already fails over between mirrors, and the requests go directly to the mirrors without the relay (radio-browser is not in NEEDS_RELAY, 483). A retired mirror fails fast with a DNS or connection error, which surfaces as a TypeError at 518. It does not cost 12 s. The 'about 60 s' figure needs all five hosts to accept connections and then hang, which is not a realistic case. Hard-coding the list instead of using DNS discovery is a design choice, not a demonstrated defect.

rejected_issues.description: Music.setMode is dead code that duplicates, with slightly different logic, the inline mode handler in renderPop.
rejected_issues.reason: Accurate: grep finds no callers of setMode, and 1891 duplicates its logic inline. Dead code has no runtime effect, though, so this is a maintainability or cleanup note rather than a defect. Whoever wires up a mode shortcut later should delete one of the two copies.

subsystems.summary: Lines 1917-2085 hold the Setup tab, the "Test all feeds" diagnostics, the map-click probe, search, and boot. Setup is driven by a small Keys.DEFS table (1919), so adding a key mostly means adding a row. Keys live in plain text in localStorage under ow.keys (1925-1926), and the custom relay URL lives under ow.proxy. "Test all feeds" (1948-1962) runs a fixed list of 22 URLs in parallel through Net.fetch. Probe.open (1998-2015) builds a Leaflet popup and fills it from Open-Meteo, Photon or Nominatim, with an optional Overpass scan. Search (2020-2033) tries, in order: coordinates, then loaded aircraft, satellites and ships, then online ADS-B lookups, then CelesTrak by name. INIT (2037-2082) builds the UI, holds the feed scheduler until Relay.check() finishes inside Splash.run, enables the stored layers, wires keyboard and BroadcastChannel, and exposes window.OW. Two security points: with the bundled helper, the FIRMS and Windy keys never leave the machine except to their provider, because serve.py hides url= in its log and serve.js logs only the host. With a custom relay, though, both keys go to the relay, which the Setup text says never happens.

key_functions.name: Keys.DEFS
key_functions.role: Table of optional API keys (windy, aisstream, firms). Each row automatically becomes a password input in Setup.

key_functions.name: Keys.relayStatus
key_functions.role: Shows the relay on/off flag plus Relay.status() text in the Setup panel.

key_functions.name: Keys.get / Keys.set
key_functions.role: Read and write one key in the localStorage object 'ow.keys' (plain text, trimmed).

key_functions.name: Keys.build
key_functions.role: Renders the relay URL field, the key inputs and the action buttons. Save stores the keys, changes Relay.custom and re-checks the relay, then forces every enabled feed to run now. Also has Clear TLE cache and Reset layout.

key_functions.name: DIAG
key_functions.role: Hand-kept list of [name, url, isText] probe targets used by the feed test.

key_functions.name: runDiagnostics
key_functions.role: Re-checks the relay, fetches every DIAG URL in parallel through Net.fetch (20 s timeout), sorts the results and shows ok / blocked / error with response times.

key_functions.name: buildSetup
key_functions.role: Writes the Setup tab HTML: Helper & keys, Test all feeds, map-reading help with keyboard list, and a static Sources & terms table. Then calls Keys.build and wires the test button.

key_functions.name: Probe.open
key_functions.role: Click-on-open-ground popup: position, sun elevation, nearest aircraft, Open-Meteo weather, Photon reverse geocode with Nominatim fallback, plus buttons for OSM scan (scanArea at 1561), aircraft bubble and copy.

key_functions.name: search submit handler
key_functions.role: Resolves a query in order: coordinates, loaded aircraft, loaded satellite (exact, then substring), loaded ship, online ADS-B hex or callsign/registration lookup (Air.get), CelesTrak name search (Sats.searchByName).

key_functions.name: INIT block
key_functions.role: Attaches panel elements, builds Setup, layer UI and presets, and pauses the scheduler (Feeds.paused = true) until the relay check is done.

key_functions.name: Splash.run
key_functions.role: Awaits Relay.check, un-pauses feeds, logs the relay state, then polls five watched layers for up to 6 s to print boot lines.

key_functions.name: Splash.close
key_functions.role: Hides the splash, starts or skips music, shows the Welcome screen on first visit.

key_functions.name: keydown handler
key_functions.role: Global shortcuts (1-5 presets, M, I, A, N, S, /, Esc, L, P). Ignored while typing in input fields.

key_functions.name: BroadcastChannel duplicate-tab warning
key_functions.role: Warns when a second copy of the page is open, because the shared per-IP rate limits would be split.

key_functions.name: window.OW
key_functions.role: Console handle exposing internal modules for tinkering.

key_functions.name: Relay.check / Relay.wrap (cross-ref)
key_functions.role: check() pings the local /proxy route, but returns true without testing when a custom relay is set. wrap() puts the whole target URL into the relay URL.

subsystems.extension_points: New API key: add {id, name, note, url} to Keys.DEFS (1919). The input, saving and escaping come for free. Read the key in the layer's feed fetch with Keys.get(id), as at 1549 (FIRMS), 1492 (Windy) and 1515 (aisstream). If the provider sends no CORS headers you must edit three hand-synced allowlists: NEEDS_RELAY (483), ALLOWED_HOSTS in serve.js (lines 11-21) and serve.py (12-22). Header-based auth also needs the header added to FORWARD_HEADERS in both helpers (serve.js 22, serve.py 23), and any custom relay must forward it too. New feed-test entry: append [name, url, isText] to DIAG (1948). The tuple cannot carry headers or a key, so testing keyed providers means turning entries into functions that build the URL and options from Keys. New credit or terms line: edit the static HTML table at 1977-1991. New keyboard shortcut: the keydown chain at 2066-2071, plus a manual update to the help text at 1972. New boot status line: add [layerId, label] to `watch` at 2052. New search resolver: insert a step in the 2020-2033 chain. Order matters and there is no resolver registry. New probe field: add a <dt>/<dd id> to the template at 2003 and an async Net.json fill like 2010-2014, scoped to `el`. New module: define it before INIT (2037). Layers register themselves through Layers.add plus feed() and are enabled at 2064. Expose the module on window.OW (2082) for debugging. What makes this easy: Keys.DEFS and DIAG are data-driven, Net.fetch handles relaying and per-host throttling transparently, and Layers.add/feed() is a clean pattern. What makes it hard: everything sits in one 2085-line script with very long single-line functions and inline HTML template strings. The relay allowlist exists in three copies. Feed-test URLs duplicate the real feed URLs. Help text, tab names and README instructions are static and already out of sync. Boot order depends on top-level statements running in sequence.

data_sources.name: NASA FIRMS (key in URL path, via relay)
Overpass API (diag status; probe OSM scan via scanArea)

subsystems.quality_notes: This range does its job and is reasonably careful. Everything inserted into the DOM is escaped (Keys.build, the test results table, Splash.line, the probe's nearest-aircraft link). Key inputs are password fields with autocomplete off. Neither bundled helper writes the FIRMS key to its log: serve.py hides url=, serve.js logs only the host. The data-driven pieces (Keys.DEFS, DIAG, the boot `watch` list) make small additions cheap. The weak points are mostly about the relay and about trust. A custom relay is accepted without validation or a test, then reported as healthy everywhere, and it receives the FIRMS and Windy keys, which contradicts the promise in the Setup text. The boot path depends on the order of top-level statements: the Leaflet fallback at 2079 is dead code, and modules must be defined before line 2037. Search is a hand-ordered chain with early returns, so precedence bugs creep in (satellite substring before ships, hex regex before callsign). Its errors are swallowed, which makes failures look like 'no match'. Maintenance cost comes from very long single-line functions with inline HTML. The relay allowlist exists in three copies (html 483, serve.js 11-21, serve.py 12-22) and FORWARD_HEADERS in two. The test URLs duplicate the real feed URLs. Help, tab and README text is static and already out of sync ('Sources tab'). One UX note outside the range: the map click handler (823-827) opens a new probe whenever no object is hit, so clicking the map to dismiss a probe opens another one and sends two more geocode and weather requests. Verdict: buildable on, but before adding more relayed or keyed sources it would pay to (1) ping-test custom relays and warn that keys pass through them, (2) generate the relay allowlist from a single source, and (3) make the feed test reuse each feed's own URL builder and throttle lane.

confirmed_issues.description: The Setup text promises that keys are "sent only to the provider that issued them", but with a custom relay the FIRMS and Windy keys are sent to the relay operator. The FIRMS key also ends up in the relay URL's query string, which typically lands in access logs.
confirmed_issues.evidence: NEEDS_RELAY (483) includes 'firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov' and 'api.windy.com'. Net.fetch (510) sends every such URL through Relay.wrap (489), which builds base + encodeURIComponent(fullUrl). The FIRMS URL has the key in its path: `/api/area/csv/${encodeURIComponent(key)}/...` (1549). Windy sends the key as the `x-windy-api-key` header (1479), which goes to the relay host. Scenario: the user follows the suggestion at 1928 and enters `https://someones-relay.workers.dev/?url={url}`. Every FIRMS poll then requests `...workers.dev/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffirms...%2Fapi%2Farea%2Fcsv%2F<MAP_KEY>%2F...`, so the relay operator and its logs get the key. Line 1938 also accepts plain `http://` relays with no check, which sends both keys over the network unencrypted. The bundled local helper is fine: serve.py's log_message hides url=, and serve.js logs only the hostname.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Line 1930 says keys are sent only to the issuing provider, but NEEDS_RELAY (483) includes firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov and api.windy.com. Net.fetch (510) routes those hosts through Relay.wrap (489), and base() (487) prefers the custom relay. The FIRMS key is in the URL path (1550), so it ends up inside the relay's ?url= query string. The Windy key goes as the x-windy-api-key header (1479) to the relay host. Line 1938 accepts any string, including http://. Lowered to low: the panel only invites a relay you host yourself (1928), the bundled helpers stay on 127.0.0.1, and the 'someone else's relay' case is the reviewer's guess. The concrete defect is a false privacy statement.

confirmed_issues.description: A custom relay URL is never checked. Relay.check() returns true as soon as Relay.custom is non-empty, so Setup, the boot splash and the feed test all report the relay as working even when the URL is wrong or dead. The custom value also silently replaces a working local helper.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Relay.check (492): `if (this.custom) { this.available = true; return true; }`. base() (487) prefers custom over the local /proxy. Save (1938) calls Relay.check() and then relayStatus(), which shows '● relay active · custom relay set' (1924). Splash.run (2048-2049) prints 'custom relay' as ok. The test footer (1960) says 'Relay is active'. Scenario: the user mistypes the Worker URL or leaves out `{url}` and `?url=`. Wrap then appends the encoded target straight onto the host, e.g. `https://x.workers.devhttps%3A%2F%2F...`. Every relayed feed (aircraft, NHC, GDELT, FIRMS, Windy) fails with 'relay unreachable', while every status indicator says the relay is fine, and the bundled helper running on 127.0.0.1 is ignored.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Relay.check (492) returns true whenever custom is non-empty and never pings it. relayStatus (1924), the splash (2049) and the diagnostics footer (1960) then all report the relay as active. Wrap (489) appends the encoded target with no separator when {url} is missing, so 'https://x.workers.dev' becomes an invalid host and every relayed feed fails with 'relay unreachable'. Two things soften it: each failing layer still shows '✕ relay unreachable (custom relay set)' in the rail, and custom overriding the local helper is documented ('Leave empty to use the local helper automatically', 1929). The defect is the status indicator that is never checked. Low.

confirmed_issues.description: The fallback for 'Leaflet failed to load' can never run. The script crashes on its first use of L, long before this check, so when the CDN is blocked or the machine is offline the user sees the boot splash stuck on 'booting' with no explanation.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Line 533 runs `const map = L.map('map', ...)` at the top level. If cdnjs (396) fails, it throws ReferenceError: L is not defined and the rest of the inline script stops. That includes `if (typeof L === 'undefined') { document.body.innerHTML = ... }` at 2079 and the window 'error' listener at 2078, which is registered too late to see the error anyway. The #splash markup (389-394) stays on screen showing 'booting' forever.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Line 533 runs `L.map(...)` at the top level of the single inline script that starts at 398. If cdnjs (396) fails to load, a ReferenceError stops the script there. The typeof L check (2079) and the error listener (2078) never run, and neither do the splash button listeners (2058). The static #splash markup (389-394) stays on 'booting' with no explanation. Only tickClock (529) runs, before the crash. Lowered to low because the app cannot work without Leaflet anyway; only the explanation is lost.

confirmed_issues.description: Any 6-character query made only of hex characters is looked up as an ICAO hex code and never as a callsign or registration. Valid callsigns such as Air China's 'CCA981' or Air Canada's 'ACA123' therefore cannot be found unless that aircraft is already loaded on the map.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `const lookups = /^[0-9a-f]{6}$/i.test(q) ? [['hex', q.toLowerCase()]] : [['callsign', ...], ['reg', ...]]`. Searching 'CCA981' while the flight is outside the loaded bubble runs only GET /v2/hex/cca981, which returns nothing. The callsign lookup is skipped, CelesTrak NAME=CCA981 returns nothing, and the toast says 'No aircraft, satellite or ship matched'.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Line 2028 tests /^[0-9a-f]{6}$/i and, on a match, runs only the hex lookup. 'CCA981' and 'ACA123' are made only of hex characters, so Air.get('hex', ...) runs /v2/hex/cca981 and the callsign and registration lookups are skipped. Line 2023 finds such a callsign only if the aircraft is already in Dyn.air. Narrow (6-character all-hex callsigns), but real.

confirmed_issues.description: Online aircraft lookups swallow every error except 'blocked/no helper'. Rate-limit cooldowns and response-shape errors are reported to the user as 'no match'.
confirmed_issues.evidence: The catch only toasts when the message matches /blocked by browser|no helper/. Air.get (864, 871) throws 'cooling down after rate limit' when a 429 has paused the sources, and the user then sees 'No aircraft ... matched' (2032). Line 2029 also reads `d.ac[0].hex`, while Air.ingest (879) accepts either `data.ac` or `data.aircraft` and skips entries without a position (881). A response that uses `aircraft` throws a TypeError, which is swallowed. If ac[0] has no position but another entry does, the matching aircraft is never opened.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed for the cooldown case. When every source is cooling down, Air.get (864-877) throws 'adsb.lol: cooling down…'. The catch at 2030 toasts only for /blocked by browser|no helper/, so the search falls through to 'No aircraft, satellite or ship matched' (2032), which is misleading. A throw from the callsign lookup also skips the registration lookup. The `aircraft`-key part is speculative: all three configured sources return `ac`. The ac[0]-without-position case needs several results for one callsign, which is rare.

confirmed_issues.description: The satellite substring match runs before the ship match and before the online aircraft lookup, so any query that appears inside a loaded satellite name opens that satellite instead.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `Dyn.sats.find(s => s.name.toLowerCase().includes(ql))` returns early. Scenario: a Baltic ship named 'COSMOS' is in Dyn.ships, and a satellite like 'COSMOS 2251 DEB' is loaded. Searching 'cosmos' opens the satellite; line 2025 (ships) and 2028 (online aircraft) never run. Short queries such as 'star' always land on the first Starlink.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Line 2024 returns on the first satellite whose name merely contains the query, before line 2025 checks ships by exact name and before the online aircraft lookup. A ship whose exact name is the query loses to a substring match in Dyn.sats. The scenarios are niche (a ship and a loaded satellite sharing a word), but an exact match being pre-empted by a substring match in another category is a real ranking defect.

confirmed_issues.description: 'Save keys' forces every enabled feed to refetch at once, not just the three keyed layers. Each click re-downloads daily and slow-cadence data, including the multi-MB submarine cable GeoJSON, and spends rate-limited budgets (GDELT, OpenSky, ADS-B).
confirmed_issues.evidence: `for (const l of Layers.defs) if (l.on && l.feed) l.feed.nextAt = 0;` sets nextAt to 0 for cables and landing points (interval 86400, 1433/1435), GDELT news (900), EONET, GDACS, NHC and so on. Clicking Save three times while adjusting a key triggers three full refetches of everything, even when no key changed.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. Line 1939 sets nextAt=0 on every enabled feed. The scheduler (781-784) then runs them all on the next tick, whether or not any key or the relay changed. Daily feeds such as cables and landing points (1433/1435, interval 86400, multi-MB GeoJSON) are re-downloaded if enabled, and news, OpenSky and others spend budget. Satellites mostly use the TLE cache (1235), and f.running stops overlapping runs, but repeated Saves still repeat the full refetch. Low performance and politeness issue.

confirmed_issues.description: The Digitraffic AIS test URL's `from=` timestamp is fixed when the page loads. A test run hours later asks for every vessel update since page load, so the response grows with how long the page has been open.
confirmed_issues.evidence: `['Digitraffic AIS', 'https://meri.digitraffic.fi/api/ais/v1/vessels?from=' + Date.now()]` is built once when DIAG is defined at the top level, not when the test runs.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. DIAG is a top-level const (1948), so `'...vessels?from=' + Date.now()` (1953) is fixed when the page loads, and later runs ask for every update since then. The impact is bounded and minor. The response can grow at most to the full vessel list, and the real ships feed already downloads that full list (no `from`) every 30 minutes (1507). The probe slowly stops being lightweight, but nothing breaks.

confirmed_issues.description: 'Reset layout & layers' deletes the custom relay URL (ow.proxy) but keeps the API keys stored right next to it. After the reload, relayed feeds quietly fall back to the local helper, or show as blocked.
confirmed_issues.evidence: The filter deletes every 'ow.*' key except 'ow.keys' and 'ow.tle.*', which includes 'ow.proxy' (written by Store.set('proxy', px) at 1938). Both settings live in the same 'Helper & keys' panel, but only the keys survive.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. The Reset filter (1942) removes every 'ow.*' key except 'ow.keys*' and 'ow.tle.*'. That includes 'ow.proxy', written via Store.set('proxy', px) at 1938. A 'Reset layout & layers' button quietly drops the custom relay setting while keeping the API keys in the same panel. After the reload, base() (487) falls back to the local helper, or to blocked when the page is opened as a file.

confirmed_issues.description: Some user-facing instructions point to a tab that does not exist.
confirmed_issues.evidence: The toast says 'Aircraft lookups need the helper running (see Sources tab)'. The tabs are Brief, Detail, Log and Setup (371-374). 'Sources & terms' is a collapsible section inside Setup (1973). README.txt also says 'Sources tab -> "Test all feeds"'.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed. The toast at 2030 says 'see Sources tab', but the tabs are Brief, Detail, Log and Setup (371-374), and 'Sources & terms' is a collapsible section inside Setup (1973). README.txt also says 'Sources tab -> "Test all feeds"', while Test all feeds is a section in Setup (1967). The user is sent to a UI element that does not exist. Trivial, but real.

confirmed_issues.description: 'Clear cached orbital data' and 'Reset layout & layers' use localStorage directly without the try/catch that Store uses everywhere else. Where storage access throws, these buttons fail with an uncaught error.
confirmed_issues.evidence: Store.get/set/del (444-446) wrap localStorage in try/catch. Lines 1941-1942 call localStorage.length and localStorage.key(i) directly. If the browser blocks site data and localStorage access throws, clicking either button throws and does nothing visible.
confirmed_issues.verification: Confirmed but trivial. Lines 1941-1942 read localStorage.length and localStorage.key() directly, while Store (444-446) and every other use go through try/catch. In Chromium with site data blocked, the localStorage getter throws SecurityError, so the handler aborts before toast() or location.reload(). The impact is minimal: with storage blocked nothing was persisted, so the only visible effect is that Reset does not reload the page to the defaults.

rejected_issues.description: 'Test all feeds' fires all 22 requests at once without the per-host throttle lanes the real feeds use. This can trip the very rate limits the app is designed to respect, and the aircraft feed is then paused.
rejected_issues.reason: It is true that the diagnostic requests skip throttle lanes (1958), but the claimed consequences are speculative. The app already sends out-of-lane ADS-B requests: user lookups use their own `src:lookup` lane (870) alongside the sweep lane, so one extra request per host per test run is the same pattern. Diag errors never call Air.on429, so the test cannot pause a source. Pausing would need the next sweep request to also get a 429, which is unproven. A GDELT rate-limit reply would only mark the test's own GDELT row as an error. The news feed's next poll is 15 minutes later (1339), so the feed is not affected.

rejected_issues.description: The DIAG list copies feed URLs by hand and has already drifted. It cannot test the keyed providers, so a user has no way to check a key they entered.
rejected_issues.reason: This is a coverage and maintainability observation, not a defect with a concrete failure. Requesting README.md on raw.githubusercontent.com is a sensible lightweight reachability check that avoids the multi-MB cable-geo.json. The SWPC host is covered by the K-index check. The keyed feeds can be checked by turning on the layer: an error shows as '✕ <err>' in the rail (UI.refreshLayer, 747) and in the Log, so 'no way to check a key' is overstated.

rejected_issues.description: Keys are stored in plain text in localStorage, which is scoped per origin. Keys entered with the page opened as a file are not visible when it is opened through the helper (and localhost:8787 is yet another origin). In Chromium-based browsers, file:// pages typically share one storage origin, so other local HTML files opened in the same browser could read 'ow.keys'.
rejected_issues.reason: For a backend-less single-file app, localStorage is the expected place for user-entered keys, and the UI says so ('stored only in this browser (localStorage)', 1930). Keys being separate per origin (file vs 127.0.0.1 vs localhost) is normal browser behavior, not a code defect. The attack needs the user to open a malicious local HTML file in the same browser, and the keys are free-tier provider keys. No concrete defect in the code.

liveness.summary:
I sent one or two real requests to every external endpoint the app uses (Bash/curl, 20 s timeout, never more than 2 per host). No personal data was sent; ipapi was tested with 8.8.8.8. Of 45 checks, 36 are up and return the fields the code reads. Raw response bodies and headers are saved in the scratchpad under ...\81fb2c50-baa5-48a8-bbab-6ce7b21ac82b\scratchpad\feeds\.

Problems to fix, in priority order:

1. **RainViewer IR satellite layer is dead (line 1408).** weather-maps.json now returns satellite.infrared: [], so the 'Cloud cover (IR satellite)' layer always fails with 'no satellite frames'.

2. **RainViewer radar shows grey boxes when zoomed in (line 1407).** Zoom 9 tiles come back as HTTP 200 with a static 'Zoom Level Not Supported' image, but the code sets maxNativeZoom: 12. Zoom 3 tiles are real. The true limit is between 3 and 9 (reportedly 7) and needs checking before lowering it.

3. **Submarine cable data is out of date (lines 1425-1426).**
   - The GitHub mirror loaded first has 510 cables; the live TeleGeography file has 733, and 275 live cable IDs are missing from the mirror.
   - The live fallback (www.submarinecablemap.com) sends no CORS header and is in neither NEEDS_RELAY (line 483) nor the helper's ALLOWED_HOSTS. In a browser it can never succeed.
   - Fix: add the host to both lists and try it first. Landing points come from the same mirror and have the same gap.

4. **The GDACS layer shows about 1-2 days, not 14 (line 1287).** The SEARCH call returned exactly 100 features, all with a todate of 2026-09-30 or later, and 59 of them are Green wildfires. Orange or Red events that ended earlier in the window are dropped. Page through the results or request alertlevel=Orange;Red.

5. **Three of five radio-browser hosts are gone (line 1826).** nl1, at1 and fi1 no longer resolve in DNS. de1 and de2 point to the same IP, so there is no real fallback.

6. **The relay lists are out of date.**
   - GDELT now sends ACAO *, so it can be dropped from NEEDS_RELAY and News would work without the helper.
   - api.adsb.one (line 483 and both helpers) and tle.ivanstanojevic.me are listed but never called.
   - celestrak.org is in the helper allowlist but is fetched directly (it has ACAO *).

7. **Smaller things to watch:**
   - Singapore's v1 traffic-images endpoint reports 'healthy' but returned only 8 cameras.
   - Planespotters returns 403 to anything that doesn't look like a browser. It's fine from the page, but don't send it through the helper unless the UA includes a contact URL.
   - adsb.fi's point endpoint returns {aircraft} while its sqk endpoint returns {ac}. Air.ingest handles both, but line 2029 (search) reads only d.ac[0], and I didn't test adsb.fi's search lookups.
   - The README says radio comes from SomaFM, but the code uses radio-browser.

**Relay list check (NEEDS_RELAY, line 483):** for adsb.lol, adsb.fi, OpenSky, NHC and NYC DOT the relay is still needed. None send a usable CORS header; OpenSky's is fixed to its own domain.

**Working with no changes needed:** USGS, both EONET calls, NWS, SWPC aurora and Kp, Open-Meteo, Photon, Nominatim, Overpass, SondeHub, both Digitraffic AIS calls, TfL, Caltrans, Fintraffic cameras and images, CelesTrak, all basemap tiles (Esri, OSM, OpenTopoMap, both NASA GIBS layers) and the CDNs (Leaflet, satellite.js, Google Fonts). SWPC's Kp file is now objects only, which line 1390 already handles. EONET labels its JSON as rss+xml, which does no harm.

**Need a key (I didn't use one):** Windy (403 'Missing x-windy-api-key'), NASA FIRMS (400 'Invalid MAP_KEY.') and aisstream (WebSocket handshake accepted from a browser origin) are all up. airplanes.live returns 403 because it needs written permission; the code already treats it as opt-in.

**Can you build on it:** yes. The feed layer is in reasonable shape. The breakage is in a few specific places and each is a small change; nothing needs restructuring.
